properties.title: Overview

properties.text:
A Python tool, `sdd`, that turns a spec-driven repo into a live Relate graph that agents query instead of re-reading Markdown.

Pipeline: **Markdown + code + git → parse (changed files only) → one Relate directory store → MCP tools for agents, JSON API + dashboard for people → write-back of task status and deviations to Markdown**.

Parts (one Python package, [SPEC-01](SPEC-01-architecture.md)):
- `daemon`: the **only** process that opens the store for writing. Watches files, syncs, serves MCP (`/mcp`), the JSON API (`/api`) and the dashboard (`/`) on `127.0.0.1:8770`.
- `public`: a separate, read-only process for the hosted demo. Opens a read-only snapshot of the store. No MCP, no writes.
- `cli`: `sdd …` for humans and CI. Talks to the daemon when it runs; otherwise reads a snapshot directly.
- `web`: a plain static dashboard (HTML + JS + Cytoscape.js), served by both `daemon` and `public`.
properties.title: What we build

properties.text:
- **Project**: one repo with SDD docs. One project = one store at `<repo>/.sdd/graph/`.
- **Spec**: a `SPEC-NN-*.md` file. **Section**: one heading inside it, with its own text, so an agent can load §5.2 alone.
- **Acceptance check**: a numbered item in a spec's *Acceptance checks* section. Tests are named after it (`test_spec03_ac06_…`, `Spec06_Ac02…`).
- **Milestone**: an `M<nn>[a-z]-*.md` file. **Task**: one checkbox line in it, with a stable ID such as `M02.3` ([SPEC-03 §4](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#4-milestones-and-tasks)).
- **Deviation**: a `D<nnn>-*.md` file plus its index row and spec notes.
- **Claim**: an agent's exclusive hold on a task. Claims live only in the graph.
- **Context packet**: what `get_context(task)` returns: the task, its milestone, the sections to read with the deviations that amend them, upstream outcomes and related code ([SPEC-05 §4](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#4-get_context)).
- **Feature / Domain**: author-declared groupings that tie specs to files and tables ([SPEC-03 §3.3](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#33-feature-line)).
- **Write-back**: the daemon editing Markdown on an agent's behalf (tick a box, write a deviation).
- **Graph-only state**: claims, agents and events, including what events record (completion notes, files touched, `AFFECTS`). Everything else can be rebuilt from Markdown, code and git.
properties.title: Concepts

properties.text:
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Relate | Embedded property-graph database by Neo4j (`pip install relate-db`, `import relate`), Cypher queries, single-process store |
| Directory store | Relate's default storage: WAL + shards in a directory. Needed for snapshots and `relate clone` |
| `.rl` | Relate's single-file store, made with `relate clone` |
| MCP | Model Context Protocol. Claude Code reaches the daemon over streamable HTTP |
| Read-only snapshot | `relate.connect(path, read_only=True)`: loads once, refuses writes, sees new data only after reopen (verified 2026-11-21) |
| Sample project | The demo repo under `samples/` with specs, milestones, deviations, code and a committed store ([SPEC-11 §5](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#5-sample-project)) |
| Replay | Simulated agents working the sample project in a loop, for the live demo |
| Reference projects | `D:\Works\ai\office-rag` and `D:\Works\ai\office-suite-v2`: real SDD repos whose format we parse. **Read-only** |

properties.title: Spec map

properties.text: These apply everywhere. A rule here beats any other spec, and a conflict is a deviation ([DEVIATIONS](../DEVIATIONS.md)).
properties.title: Global conventions

properties.text:
1. Specs are the source of truth. Code that disagrees with a spec is either a bug or a logged deviation.
2. **SPEC-02 owns every label and relationship type.** A new one is a SPEC-02 change in the same change as the code.
3. **SPEC-05 indexes every MCP tool, SPEC-07 every HTTP endpoint, SPEC-08 every CLI command.**
4. Milestones are worked in number order, one at a time; a milestone's *Read first* line lists the sections to load.
5. **Markdown is the product's source of truth too.** The graph holds nothing that cannot be rebuilt from Markdown, code and git, except graph-only state ([§2](#2-concepts)).
properties.title: Source of truth

properties.text:
- Python 3.13, package `sdd` in `src/sdd/`, distribution name `relate-sdd`, CLI `sdd`.
- Node IDs are human-readable strings, never generated UUIDs: `SPEC-03`, `SPEC-03#5.2`, `M02`, `M02.3`, `D012`, `file:src/sdd/cli.py` ([SPEC-02 §1](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#1-ids-and-common-properties)). The one exception is Event IDs (`event:<ulid>`): events are graph-only and have no natural key.
- Timestamps are UTC ISO 8601 strings with `Z` in the graph and JSON. The dashboard shows them in the browser's zone.
- JSON fields are `snake_case` everywhere (API, MCP, exports). Enumerations are lowercase strings (`todo`, `claimed`, `done`).
- Paths in the graph are POSIX, relative to the project root.
properties.title: Names and formats

properties.text:
- **Only `sdd/graph/store.py` imports `relate`.** Everything else uses its functions.
- **All graph writes go through the write queue** in `sdd/graph/store.py` ([SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)).
- **All Markdown writes go through `sdd/sync/writeback.py`.**
- MCP tools, HTTP routes and CLI commands only validate input, call one function in `sdd/service/`, and map the result. **No Cypher outside `sdd/graph/` and `sdd/service/`.**
- Parsers are pure: text in, parsed objects out. No I/O, no graph access.
properties.title: Layering

properties.text:
- One error shape for MCP, HTTP and CLI `--json`: `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "details"}}`. Codes are stable `snake_case` ([SPEC-05 §8](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#8-error-codes)).
- Messages say what happened and what to do next ("Task M02.3 is claimed by sonnet-2 since 10:42. Pick another from next_tasks.").
properties.title: Errors

properties.text:
- The daemon binds to loopback only. MCP and every write path are never reachable from the public process ([SPEC-09](SPEC-09-security.md)).
- Arbitrary Cypher runs only through the query guard, in a transaction that is always rolled back.
properties.title: Security

properties.text:
- Every numbered acceptance check in a spec becomes a test named after it: `test_spec05_ac03_double_claim_one_winner` ([SPEC-10 §1](SPEC-10-testing-and-benchmark.md#1-conventions)).
- Tests never touch the network or the reference projects. They use fixture repos under `tests/fixtures/`.
- Full gates: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`, `pytest`.
properties.title: Tests

properties.text:
- All building, testing and running happens **in Docker** (`docker compose exec dev …`). Nothing is installed on the Windows host ([SPEC-11 §1](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#1-development-container)).
- File watching defaults to **polling** inside containers, because inotify does not see Windows-host edits through a bind mount (verified 2026-11-21).
properties.title: Development environment

properties.text:
1. `docker compose up` on a clean machine starts the daemon on the sample project, and the dashboard shows its graph within 60 s of the images being built.
2. The parser indexes both reference formats (fixtures that mirror office-rag and office-suite-v2 with invented content) with zero unparsed task lines and zero unresolved spec links that resolve on GitHub.
3. Ten parallel simulated agents claiming tasks produce **zero** double claims and zero lost checkbox updates.
4. On the sample project, the average `get_context` packet is **at least 70 % smaller** than the Markdown an agent reads by the token rule for the same task ([SPEC-10 §5](SPEC-10-testing-and-benchmark.md#5-benchmark)).
5. `impact("attachments")` (or the sample's equivalent table) returns specs, sections, features, files, tasks and deviations, each with the path that connects it.
6. The repo ships committed stores (a checkpointed snapshot directory + `.rl`, made by `sdd snapshot`; the live `.sdd/graph/` is never committed, [DEC-001](../decisions/DEC-001-committed-store.md)), Mermaid diagrams in the README, a live demo link and a static demo link.
7. This repo's own docs index cleanly with its own tool (dogfooding), from M03b on.

| # | Item | Owner | Status |

| O1 | Can office-suite-v2 content be published in this public repo as the sample? | User | **Closed (2026-11-21): no.** Nothing from office-suite-v2 is ever published; the sample is invented ([DEC-004](../decisions/DEC-004-sample-fallback.md), [SPEC-11 §5](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#5-sample-project)) |

| O3 | Are JSON-codec snapshots and `.rl` clones possible from Python, or only from the `relate` CLI? | M06a | **Closed (2026-11-22): only from the CLI.** The `relate-db` 1.2.0 Python package has no clone or codec API (`Connection` has `execute`, `commit`, `rollback`, `flush`, `close`, …). The `relate` CLI (in the dev image, not the runtime image) does all three: `relate clone SRC DEST.rl` (single file), `relate clone --to-snapshot-format json SRC DEST` (directory with a readable `graph.json`) and `relate clone SRC DEST` (directory copy). A clone reads what was committed when it opened and works beside a running writer; its output holds `.cypherlite.writer` files (dropped) and keeps the `.cypherlite.lock` markers ([D001](../deviations/D001-store-copies-keep-lock-markers.md)); `relate.connect(…, read_only=True)` opens all three. **`graph/store.py`:** the only module that runs the CLI (`clone`, `copy_store` as the fallback without it); `sdd snapshot` ([SPEC-08 §3](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#3-exports-and-snapshots)) |
| O4 | Does `relate-db` support a per-query timeout or row cap from Python? | M03b | **Closed (2026-11-22): no.** `relate-db` 1.2.0 has neither: `connect()` and `execute()` take no timeout, and `execute()` builds the whole result before `fetchmany()` returns (a single value over the engine's expression-memory limit fails with `DataError`). **`service/query_guard.py`:** the fallback of [SPEC-09 §3](SPEC-09-security.md#3-query-guard) step 3: the query runs on a worker thread that holds a per-process gate until it really ends; the caller gets `query_timeout` after 5 s; the row cap is applied by fetching at most 101 rows |
| O5 | Is one `Connection` safe for concurrent reads from several threads, and does a read on it during an open write transaction see uncommitted data? | M00b | **Closed (2026-11-21): no, connections are thread-affine.** `relate-db` 1.2.0 declares DB-API `threadsafety = 1`; a call from any thread other than the opening one raises `ProgrammingError` (`WrongThread`). A read on the connection inside an open transaction does see that transaction's own uncommitted writes. **`store.py`:** its worker thread opens the connection and runs every job, reads included, one at a time in submission order, each in its own transaction, so a read never sees another job's writes ([SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)) |
| O6 | Does Relate Cypher support uniqueness constraints, property indexes and full-text indexes? | M00b | **Closed (2026-11-21): yes, all three.** Neo4j 5 syntax with `IF NOT EXISTS` (idempotent), created inside a transaction and rolled back with it. A duplicate raises `IntegrityError` (`ConstraintVerificationFailed`), also within one statement. Full-text is queried with `CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes(name, text)` (the `SEARCH … FULLTEXT` clause does not parse). `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` / `SHOW INDEXES`, `db.labels()` work. **`graph/schema.py`:** a unique `id` on every label, the five property indexes and both full-text indexes ([SPEC-02 §6](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#6-indexes-and-constraints)) |
| O7 | Can browser.neo4j.io (HTTPS) connect to a local `relate serve --bolt`? | M99 (bonus) | Open |
| O8 | Can Relate's `fs-to-graph` / `git-to-graph` extensions write into a store our daemon owns? | M04a | **Closed (2026-11-22): no, keep our walker and git reader.** `relate` 1.2.0 has `relate extension install\|list` and `relate run <name> -d PATH`; `run` says "the child walks its source and emits rows over the wire; the host alone owns the store". No extension is installed, and installing one fetches from the network. So an extension can only write into a store the `relate` host opens itself, which the daemon's writer lock prevents ([SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)). **`sync/files.py`, `sync/git.py`:** the walker and the git reader ([SPEC-04 §4, §6](SPEC-04-sync.md#4-code-walker)) |
| O9 | Relate CLI install in the Docker image (install script, amd64 + arm64) | M00a | **Closed (2026-11-21).** The `relate-db` 1.2.0 wheel ships no CLI binary. The `dev` stage runs the official `https://relatedb.ai/install.sh` with `HOME=/opt/relate` and links `/opt/relate/.local/bin/relate` to `/usr/local/bin/relate`. The script picks amd64/arm64 from `uname`, verifies the signed `SHA256SUMS` with `ssh-keygen` (so the stage adds `openssh-client`) and always installs the latest release (no pin option). CLI telemetry is on by default; the image sets `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` ([SPEC-11 §1](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#1-development-container)) |
| O10 | Can node and relationship properties hold maps (`Spec.header`, `Event.data`)? | M00b | **Closed (2026-11-21): no.** A map, or a list holding lists or maps, raises `DataError` (`InvalidPropertyType`) on nodes and relationships; flat lists, empty lists, `null`, bool, int, float work. Maps as *parameters* (`UNWIND $rows`) work. **`store.py`:** `encode_props()` stores such values as JSON strings under `<name>_json` (`header_json`, `data_json`); every result is decoded on the way out (nodes, relationships, `properties()`, columns named `*_json`), so callers see `header` as a map |
| O11 | Can a `read_only=True` connection open a store on a **read-only mount** (no lock files created)? Does a crashed writer leave a stale `.cypherlite.writer` lock that blocks the next open? | M00b | **Closed (2026-11-21): yes; no stale lock.** A read-only open creates and writes no file and works on a `:ro` mount, **but only if the `.cypherlite.lock` markers exist** in the store root and in `wal/` (content is irrelevant; `.cypherlite.writer` is not needed). Without them it fails with "read-only open requires an existing database / WAL". The writer lock is an OS lock: a SIGKILLed writer leaves the files, but the next writable open succeeds at once. A read-only open never creates a missing store. A read-only connection refuses a write in autocommit mode, but **inside a transaction it accepts the write and refuses only at commit**, so the always-rollback rule of [SPEC-09 §3](SPEC-09-security.md#3-query-guard) is load-bearing. **`store.py`:** `exists()` checks the markers; a read-only open of a store without them fails with `invalid_input` naming them; `sdd snapshot` and the `.gitignore` keep them ([D001](../deviations/D001-store-copies-keep-lock-markers.md), [SPEC-08 §3](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#3-exports-and-snapshots)) |
| O12 | Can one process hold the writable connection **and** open a `read_only=True` snapshot of the same store? (Used for guarded queries, [SPEC-09 §3](SPEC-09-security.md#3-query-guard)) | M00b | **Closed (2026-11-21): yes.** The snapshot opens next to the writer (same or another process, on any thread), holds every *committed* transaction, flushed or not, and nothing uncommitted. It loads once and does not follow later commits. Opening takes about 20 ms at 20k nodes. **`store.py`:** `read_snapshot()` opens a fresh read-only connection on the calling thread for each guarded query (thread affinity rules out sharing one), runs it in a rolled-back transaction and closes it; it never waits behind the write queue. In-memory and read-only stores run it as a rolled-back job instead |

properties.title: Architecture

properties.text:
```
docs/specs/*.md, docs/milestones/*.md, docs/deviations/*.md, code, .git   ← humans and agents edit
        │  watcher (polling in Docker) → hash → re-parse changed files only
        ▼
  sdd daemon   ONE process · sole writer of .sdd/graph/ · 127.0.0.1:8770
     ├─ /mcp     MCP streamable HTTP  ← Claude Code: orchestrator + N subagents
     ├─ /api     JSON API + /api/events (SSE)
     └─ /        dashboard (static)
        │  checkpoint
        ▼
  sdd public   separate process · read_only snapshot, reopened on change · no /mcp · :8780
```

Rules:
1. **One writable connection per store, in one process: the daemon.** Relate is a single-process engine. A second writer gets `storage locked` (verified).
2. MCP uses **HTTP on localhost, never stdio**. stdio would start one server per Claude Code session, and they would fight over the store.
3. The CLI never opens the store for writing while the daemon runs. It detects the daemon through `.sdd/daemon.json` (pid, host, port, instance, token hash, started_at, project) **plus a health call** whose `instance` must equal the file's; the file alone proves nothing, because PIDs are reused (especially inside containers) and a killed daemon leaves the file behind. The authority for "a writer exists" is Relate's own writer lock (`storage locked`). Read commands then call the API. Without a daemon, read commands open a read-only snapshot, and write commands (`sync`, `ids --write`) open the store themselves.
4. `sdd public` opens `read_only=True` and reopens when the store's `manifest.json` changes (checked every 2 s). This is how the hosted demo follows the replay writer, because Python has no live WAL follow.

```
  sync/               watcher.py, indexer.py (file → parser → upsert), files.py (code walker),

  mcp/server.py       MCP tools → service
  web/api.py          Starlette routes → service; sse.py; static/ (dashboard, vendored JS)
  cli.py              `sdd` (Typer) → service or daemon API
  daemon.py           wires store + watcher + MCP + web; public.py (read-only server)
  demo/replay.py      simulated agents (SPEC-11 §4)
tests/                pytest; fixtures/ (small repos in both reference formats)
samples/              the demo project (SPEC-11 §5)

```

properties.title: Module boundaries

properties.text:
- `store.py` owns one `relate.Connection` per process and one **worker thread** that opened it: connections are thread-affine (O5, [SPEC-00 §8](SPEC-00-overview.md#8-schedule-and-open-items)), so every use of the shared connection, reads included, runs on that thread. It exposes `write(fn)` (and `submit(fn)`, which returns a future), `read(cypher, params)`, `read_snapshot(cypher, params, limit=)` and `checkpoint()`. `Store.open(path, read_only=True)` is the read-only open for the CLI and `sdd public`; it never creates or writes a file.
- **Write queue:** every job is a function run by the worker thread, one at a time, in submission order. The connection stays in `autocommit = False`; a write job ends with `commit()`, and any job that raises with `rollback()` (verified: Cypher `BEGIN` is not supported; the connection methods are; schema statements are transactional too). A job that touches several nodes (claim, complete, re-sync of one file) is **one transaction**. A job cannot queue another job (it would deadlock); it uses the `Tx` it is given.
- On `write-write conflict` or `storage locked`, the job is rolled back and retried 3 times with 50 / 200 / 800 ms backoff, then fails with `write_conflict` (retryable). A writable open that meets `storage locked` retries on the same schedule, then fails with `daemon_running` (a killed writer leaves no stale lock, O11). With one writer thread these should be rare; the retry exists for the open race and for engine-internal conflicts. **A job must be idempotent**, because a retry runs it again from the start (including its write-back, [SPEC-04 §5.2](SPEC-04-sync.md#52-safety)).
- **Reads** are jobs on the same queue (O5): they run after every job queued before them, in a transaction that is always rolled back, so a read never sees another job's uncommitted writes and a stray write in a read changes nothing. Results are plain dicts: nodes and relationships become their properties, and `*_json` properties are decoded (O10, `encode_props()` on the way in).
- **Guarded queries** ([SPEC-09 §3](SPEC-09-security.md#3-query-guard)) never wait behind the write queue: `read_snapshot()` opens a fresh `read_only=True` connection **on the calling thread** for each query (O12; about 20 ms at 20k nodes), runs it in a rolled-back transaction and closes it. The snapshot holds every committed transaction, so no refresh after checkpoints is needed. On an in-memory or read-only store it runs as a rolled-back job on the worker thread instead.
- `checkpoint()` calls `flush()`. It runs after each sync batch and before `sdd snapshot`, so the public process and committed stores see complete data.
- Storage mode: **directory store** at `<repo>/.sdd/graph/` (durability `full`). The live store is **never committed** (gitignored): a store a daemon writes to would keep the tree dirty, conflict on every merge and change under `git checkout`. Committed copies for judges are made by `sdd snapshot` ([SPEC-08 §3](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#3-exports-and-snapshots), [DEC-001](../decisions/DEC-001-committed-store.md)).
- One store per project. No cross-store queries (Relate has none). The global lessons store is a stretch goal and holds copies only.
properties.title: Relate access and concurrency

properties.text:
1. Load config. If `.sdd/daemon.json` exists and its port answers `/api/health` for this project, refuse to start (`daemon_running`). A file whose daemon does not answer is stale and is ignored.
2. Open the store writable. `storage locked` means another process writes it: exit with `daemon_running`. Then create indexes ([SPEC-02 §6](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#6-indexes-and-constraints)).
3. **Startup sync:** full scan comparing content hashes, then git sync ([SPEC-04 §2](SPEC-04-sync.md#2-incremental-sync)).
4. Start the watcher, the git poller and the HTTP server (Uvicorn, one worker; MCP mounted with `MCPServer.streamable_http_app()` from `mcp` 2.x).
5. Write `.sdd/daemon.json` (`{pid, host, port, instance, started_at, token_sha256, project}`; `instance` is a random ID per start, answered by `/api/health`) once the socket is bound. On SIGTERM: stop the watcher, drain the write queue, checkpoint, close, remove `daemon.json`.
properties.title: Daemon lifecycle

properties.text:
Runtime: `relate-db` (≥ 1.2), `mcp` (≥ 2.3, 2.x API), `starlette`, `uvicorn`, `sse-starlette`, `markdown-it-py`, `watchdog`, `pathspec`, `typer`, `pydantic` (v2, for tool and API schemas). Dev: `pytest`, `pytest-socket`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `import-linter`. Git is called as the `git` CLI (no GitPython). Dashboard: vendored `cytoscape.min.js` (no CDN at runtime, so the hosted demo has no third-party calls).

Licences must be permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD). Relate is Apache-2.0.
properties.title: Dependencies

properties.text:
1. A second `sdd daemon` on the same project exits with `daemon_running` and leaves the first untouched.
2. With the daemon running, `sdd sync` refuses with `daemon_running`, and `sdd impact X` answers through the daemon API.
3. Without a daemon, `sdd impact X` answers from a read-only snapshot and creates no lock file.
4. A write job that raises midway leaves no partial nodes (rollback), and the next job succeeds.
5. 50 concurrent `claim_task` calls on different tasks all succeed, in queue order, with no `write_conflict` surfaced.
6. `import-linter` passes: `relate` is imported only in `graph/store.py`.

properties.text:
| Label | `id` format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `SPEC-NN` from the file name | `SPEC-03` |
| Section | `<spec>#<number>` if numbered, else `<spec>#<slug>` (deduped with `-2`, `-3`; this ID slug is ours, the GitHub `anchor` property is separate) | `SPEC-03#5.2`, `SPEC-02#attachments` |
| AcceptanceCheck | `<spec>#ac<n>` | `SPEC-03#ac6` |
| Milestone | `M<digits>[a-z]?` from the file name | `M02`, `M20f`, `M100` |
| Task | `<milestone>.<n>` from the inline ID | `M02.3`, `M20f.12` |
| Deviation | `D<nnn>` | `D012` |
| Doc | `doc:<path>` | `doc:docs/IDEA.md`, `doc:CLAUDE.md` |
| Folder / File | `dir:<path>` / `file:<path>` | `file:src/sdd/cli.py` |
| Commit | `commit:<full sha>` | |
| Table / Column | `table:<name>` / `column:<table>.<name>` | `column:attachments.owner_id` |
| Feature / Domain | `feature:<slug>` / `domain:<slug>` | `feature:file-sharing` |
| Agent | `agent:<name>` | `agent:sonnet-2` |
| Event | `event:<ulid>` | |
| Meta | `meta` (one node) | |

`ids.normalise()` accepts the forms people type: `SPEC-03 §5.2`, `SPEC-03§5.2`, `spec-03#5.2`, `SPEC-3 5.2`, `m2.3`. Rules: prefixes are upper-cased (`SPEC`, `M`, `D`) and milestone letter suffixes lower-cased; spec and milestone numbers are zero-padded to at least 2 digits (`SPEC-3` → `SPEC-03`, `m2.3` → `M02.3`, `M100` stays), deviation numbers to 3 (`d12` → `D012`); `§`, `#` or a space separates a spec from its section number, with or without spaces around `§` and `#` (`SPEC-03§5.2`, `SPEC-03 § 5.2`); a number glued straight to the spec number (`SPEC-035.2`) is rejected as ambiguous. A section slug or acceptance check takes the same separators (`SPEC-02 §attachments`, `SPEC-03 ac6`). IDs taken from file names are padded the same way, so a file `M2-x.md` is `M02`.

**Common properties** on every parsed node: `id` (unique), `source_path`, `source_line` (1-based, where applicable), `content_hash` (sha256 of the parsed text), `last_synced` (UTC ISO). Code-layer nodes have `last_synced` but no `source_line`.

properties.title: Agent, Event (graph-only)

properties.text:
Everything below is lost by `sdd sync --reset` and is excluded from rebuild equivalence ([SPEC-10 §4](SPEC-10-testing-and-benchmark.md#4-invariant-suite) invariant 2). Everything else must be reproducible from Markdown, code and git.
- Nodes: Agent, Event.
- Task properties: `claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, `completed_by`, `done_at`, `notes`.
- Relationships: `CLAIMED`, `ABOUT`, and every relationship with `src = "tool"` (§4): `TOUCHES` from `files_touched`, `COMPLETES` from `complete_task(commit=…)`.

`RAISED_IN` → Task and `AFFECTS` are **not** graph-only: `log_deviation` writes them into the deviation file, so a rebuild reproduces them ([DEC-002](../decisions/DEC-002-graph-only-links.md)).
properties.title: Graph-only state (canonical list)

properties.text:
| Label | Properties |
|---|---|
| Folder | `path`, `name` |
| File | `path`, `name`, `language` (by extension), `size`, `lines`, `content_hash`, `is_test` |
| Commit | `sha`, `short`, `message` (first line), `author`, `at`, `paths` (list, every path in the diff including deleted ones) |
| Table | `name`, `defined_in` (section id), `source_path`, `source_line` |
| Column | `table`, `name`, `type`, `nullable` (bool), `pk` (bool), `notes`, `source_path`, `source_line` |
| Feature | `name`, `slug`, `globs` (list of the `Implements` patterns, the union over every declaring spec) |
| Domain | `name`, `slug` |

Feature and Domain nodes have **no `source_path`**: several specs can declare one, so they are written from every spec's Feature lines after phase 1 (merged by ID) and deleted when no spec declares them any more. Their relationships (`SPECIFIED_BY`, `BELONGS_TO`, `USES_TABLE`) are owned by the declaring spec like any other.

File contents are **never** stored. The graph holds connections and intent; agents still read and grep files.

There is **no root Folder**: a top-level file or folder has no `CONTAINS` parent. The File properties apply to SDD documents too (the walker writes `language`, `size`, `lines` and `is_test` for every file), but only the indexer sets an SDD document's `content_hash` ([SPEC-04 §4](SPEC-04-sync.md#4-code-walker)); a code file's hash is the walker's. `language` and `lines` are absent when not known.

| Type | From → To | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `HAS_SECTION` | Spec → Section, Section → Section (nesting) | headings |
| `HAS_CHECK` | Spec → AcceptanceCheck | *Acceptance checks* section |
| `LINKS_TO` | Section \| Doc → Section \| Spec \| Milestone \| Deviation \| Doc \| File | Markdown links in section text, and in the text of a Doc ([SPEC-03 §5.3](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#53-docs)) |
| `DEPENDS_ON` | Milestone → Milestone | *Depends on* (and reversed *Blocks*) |
| `READS` | Milestone → Section \| Spec | *Read first* line; `{whole: true}` on Spec targets marked "(whole file)" |
| `INCLUDES` | Milestone → Task | checkboxes |
| `BLOCKED_BY` | Task → Task | `(after M02.1)` |
| `GOVERNED_BY` | Task → Section \| Spec | links inside the task line |
| `VERIFIES` | Task → AcceptanceCheck | `SPEC-03 §10 checks 3–9` in the task line |
| `PLANS` | Doc(plan) → Milestone | `M20f-plan.md` |
| `AMENDS` | Deviation → Section \| Spec | the **Spec:** field and every `> **DEVIATION:** see [Dnnn]` note |
| `RAISED_IN` | Deviation → Milestone \| Task | **Date / milestone:** field (milestone, then an optional task ID: `2026-11-25 · M02 · M02.3`) |
| `AFFECTS` | Deviation → File \| Table | the optional **Affects:** field (backticked file paths and table names) |
| `MENTIONS` | Section \| Task \| Deviation → Table \| File | a backticked identifier that exactly matches a table name or an existing file path |
| `CLAIMED` | Agent → Task | graph-only; `{at}` |
| `ABOUT` | Event → any | graph-only |
| `CONTAINS` | Folder → Folder \| File | walker |
| `PARENT` | Commit → Commit | git |
| `CHANGED` | Commit → File | git; `{change: A\|M\|D\|R}`; only to files that still exist |
| `COMPLETES` | Commit → Task | `[M02.3]` in the message, or `complete_task(commit=…)` |
| `PART_OF` | Commit → Milestone | `(M20f)` or `M20f` as a word in the message, when no task ID is present |
| `TOUCHES` | Task → File | `complete_task(files_touched)` and files changed by commits that complete the task |
| `TESTS` | File → AcceptanceCheck | test names matching `spec(\d+)_ac(\d+)` (case-insensitive) in test files |
| `DEFINES_TABLE` | Section → Table | schema tables ([SPEC-03 §6](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#6-schema-tables)) |
| `HAS_COLUMN` | Table → Column | |
| `REFERENCES` | Column → Table | `→ users`, `FK → documents` |
| `SPECIFIED_BY` | Feature → Spec | Feature line |
| `BELONGS_TO` | Feature → Domain | Feature line |
| `IMPLEMENTED_IN` | Feature → File | Feature line globs, re-expanded on file add/remove |
| `USES_TABLE` | Feature → Table | Feature line |

**Every relationship carries `src`**, which says who owns it and who may delete it:

| `src` | Owner | Deleted when |
|---|---|---|
| a project-relative file path | the parser of that file | that file is re-synced (all its relationships are deleted and recreated in one transaction, [SPEC-04 §2](SPEC-04-sync.md#2-incremental-sync)) or removed |
| `walker` | the code walker (`CONTAINS`, `IMPLEMENTED_IN`, `TESTS`) | the walker rebuilds them |
| `git:<sha>` | git sync (`PARENT`, `CHANGED`, `COMPLETES`, `PART_OF`, commit-derived `TOUCHES`) | that commit becomes unreachable ([SPEC-04 §6](SPEC-04-sync.md#6-git-sync)) |
| `tool` | a write tool, and `ABOUT` from sync Events (graph-only) | never by sync; only by `sdd sync --reset` or `DETACH DELETE` of an endpoint |

The same type may have several owners (`TOUCHES` from a tool and from git); each owner only ever deletes its own.
properties.title: Relationships

properties.text: A link whose target does not exist yet (a spec not written, a section renamed) creates no relationship. It is recorded on the source node as `unresolved: list<string>` and reported by `sdd doctor` and `sdd status`. The list lives on the node that is the relationship's source if the file that states the link produces it; if not (an `AMENDS` from a deviation, written as a note in a spec), on the resolved target if the file produces that, else on the file's own Spec, Milestone, Deviation or Doc node. A file with no node (the deviation index) records nothing. Each sync of a file rewrites the `unresolved` list of every node that file produces.
properties.title: Unresolved links

properties.text:
- Unique `id` on every label (`uniq_<label>_id`; Relate supports uniqueness constraints, O6). Upserts still `MERGE` on `id`; a duplicate `CREATE` fails with an integrity error.
- Property indexes on `Task.status`, `Task.milestone_id`, `File.path`, `Section.spec_id`, `Event.at` (`idx_<label>_<property>`).
- Full-text: `ft_section_text` (`Section.title + text`) and `ft_file_path` (`File.path`), queried with `CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes(name, text)` from `service/` (the query guard rejects `CALL`).
- All created by `graph/schema.py` (`ensure()`, idempotent, `IF NOT EXISTS`) when the daemon or `sdd sync` opens the store. `schema.SCHEMA_VERSION` (now 1) is the code's version; `Meta.schema_version` records the version a store was built with.

properties.title: Markdown parsing

properties.text:
1. **Parsers are pure and tolerant.** They take `(path, text)` and return parsed objects plus `warnings` (`{path, line, code, message}`). They never raise on bad Markdown. `sdd doctor` lists the warnings.
2. Parsing uses `markdown-it-py` tokens (which carry line numbers) plus small regexes for header lines. No HTML rendering.
3. **No new conventions are required except stable task IDs** ([§4.2](#42-task-ids)). The Feature line ([§3.3](#33-feature-line)) is optional.
4. Both reference formats must parse with zero warnings of severity `error`.
5. **Code is not prose.** Markdown links, spec references, task-ID mentions and `**DEVIATION:**` notes inside inline code spans and fenced or indented code blocks are ignored, so specs can show examples without creating links. Two uses of inline code are deliberate and still apply: the backticked identifier `part` of a spec reference (§2.2), and `MENTIONS` (§3.2).
6. **Warning codes.** Every warning has a `code` and a severity; `sdd doctor` exits 1 on any `error`. The complete list (`parse/model.py` `WARNING_CODES` builds every warning from it, so a typo fails fast):

| Code | Severity | When |
|---|---|---|
| `bad_filename` | error | the file name has no Spec, Milestone or Deviation ID, so the parser cannot build the node |
| `task_duplicate_id` | error | two tasks with the same stable ID in one file (the second becomes positional) |
| `missing_h1` | warning | no H1 |
| `h1_id_mismatch` | warning | the H1's ID differs from the file name's (the file name wins) |
| `task_id_mismatch` | warning | [§4.2](#42-task-ids) |
| `task_unstable_id` | warning | [§4.2](#42-task-ids) |
| `task_bad_after` | warning | `(after …)` names something that is not a task ID |
| `ref_bad_range` | warning | a `§` range that cannot be expanded (both ends are kept as plain section references) |
| `ac_duplicate_number` | warning | two acceptance checks with one number (the second is skipped) |
| `feature_bad_line` | warning | a Feature line without a name |
| `feature_glob_empty` | warning | a Feature's globs match no file; reported by `sync/` |
| `deviation_missing_section` | warning | [§5.1](#51-deviation-files) |
| `deviation_bad_field` | warning | an unparsable **Date / milestone:** date |
| `deviation_index_mismatch` | warning | [§5.2](#52-deviation-index) |
| `duplicate_id` | warning | two files produce the same node ID; the first by path wins and the later file's node is dropped ([SPEC-04 §3](SPEC-04-sync.md#3-deletes-and-renames); reported by `sync/`, not by a parser) |
| `section_duplicate_id` | info | two headings map to one section ID (the second gets `-2`) |
| `link_moved` | info | [§2.1](#21-markdown-links) (reported by the resolver) |

Default paths, overridable in `.sdd/config.toml`:

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `specs` | `docs/specs/SPEC-*.md` |
| `milestones` | `docs/milestones/**/M*.md` whose file name matches `M\d+[a-z]?-.+\.md`, excluding `*-plan.md` |
| `plans` | `docs/milestones/**/M*-plan.md` whose file name matches `M\d+[a-z]?-plan\.md` |
| `deviations` | `docs/deviations/D*.md` |
| `deviation_index` | `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` |
| `docs` | `**/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/IDEA.md`, `docs/design-system.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `README.md` |
| `schema_specs` | specs whose file name contains `schema` |
| `tests` | `tests/**`, `**/*Tests/**`, `**/*.test.ts`, `**/test_*.py`, `**/*_test.go` |
properties.title: Rules and configuration

properties.text:
A relative link is resolved against the linking file's folder to a path, then to the node with that `source_path` (Spec, Milestone, Deviation, Doc, or File). Its anchor, if any, is matched against `Section.anchor` in that spec. External links (`http…`) are ignored.

**Moved files.** If no node has that path, but the link's file name starts with a spec, milestone or deviation ID (`M00-foundation.md`, `SPEC-04-sync.md`, `D012-….md`), the link resolves to the node with that ID wherever its file now lives, with a `link_moved` warning (severity `info`). This keeps links working after `complete_milestone` moves a file to `done/`, while write-back repairs the Markdown itself ([SPEC-04 §5.1](SPEC-04-sync.md#51-edits)).
properties.title: Markdown links

properties.text:
Section references in **link text and plain text** are parsed with one grammar, used everywhere (Read first, task lines, deviation **Spec:** fields, prose):

```
ref     := "SPEC-" digits [ ws? sections ] [ "(whole file)" | "(whole section)" ]
sections:= part ( ws? ("," | "and") ws? part )*
part    := "§" num [ ws? ("–" | "-") ws? "§"? num ]  |  "`" identifier "`"
num     := digits ( "." digits )*
```

- **A reference to a section includes its descendants.** `SPEC-00 §6` means §6 and §6.1–6.7. `READS`, `GOVERNED_BY` and `LINKS_TO` point at the named section only; every reader (`get_context`, `read_section`, the benchmark) expands it to the subtree. "(whole section)" is accepted and means the same as no suffix.
- A range expands to the sibling sections between both ends, inclusive: `§3–4` → `#3`, `#4`; `§4.6–4.7` → `#4.6`, `#4.7`; `§4–§6` → `#4`, `#5`, `#6`.
- A backticked identifier names a section by the slug of its **title, numbered or not**: `` SPEC-02 `file_shares` `` → the section titled `file_shares`; `` SPEC-02 `documents` `` → the section `` ## 2. `documents` `` (ID `SPEC-02#2`). No match is an unresolved link.
- Trailing words such as `step 1` or `invariant 1` are kept in the relationship's `note` property, not resolved.
- **When a link has both an anchor and § references in its text, the text wins** (an anchor can only point at the first section of a range).
- `SPEC-NN` alone (or "(whole file)") targets the Spec node.
- References to non-spec docs (`design-system §1`) resolve to the Doc and are recorded with `note`.
properties.title: Spec-reference grammar

properties.text: The H1 is `# SPEC-NN — Title` (em dash, en dash or hyphen). The blockquote right after it is the **header**: every `**Key:** value` pair, split on ` · ` and across `>` lines, goes into `Spec.header`; `Status` and `Owner of` also go into their own properties. Both reference styles parse (`**Status:** v1 (…) · **Owner of:** …` and `**Spec ID:** SPEC-02 · **Consumed by:** …`).
properties.title: Header

properties.text:
- Every H2–H4 is a Section. A leading number (`5.2`, `6.`, `10.`) becomes `number`; the rest is `title`. `anchor` follows GitHub's slug rules.
- `text` is the body until the next heading of the same or a higher level, **excluding** child sections (they are their own nodes, linked by `HAS_SECTION`).
- A Section's `content_hash` covers its own text only, so editing §5.2 changes §5.2, not §5.
- Markdown links and spec references in the text become `LINKS_TO`. Backticked identifiers that exactly match a known table name or an existing file path (a File node, so a code file or an SDD document) become `MENTIONS`; one identifier can name both, and both are linked ([SPEC-02 §4](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#4-relationships)).
- A line containing `**DEVIATION:**` (at any blockquote depth, outside code) links every `[Dnnn]` on it to this section with `AMENDS` (from the deviation).
- A section titled *Acceptance checks* (any level, number optional) yields one AcceptanceCheck per top-level numbered list item.
properties.title: Sections

properties.text:
Optional, in the header blockquote, one line per feature:

```markdown
> **Feature:** File sharing · **Domain:** Files · **Implements:** `backend/**/FileShares/**`, `frontend/src/features/files/**` · **Tables:** file_shares, attachments
```

Yields Feature (slug from the name), Domain, `SPECIFIED_BY` this spec, `BELONGS_TO`, `IMPLEMENTED_IN` (globs expanded by sync, [SPEC-04 §4](SPEC-04-sync.md#4-code-walker)) and `USES_TABLE`. A feature declared in two specs is one node with two `SPECIFIED_BY` relationships and the union of the globs. Globs are project-relative gitignore-style patterns, like the config globs (a slash-less pattern is anchored at the root). A `USES_TABLE` to a table nobody defines is listed in `unresolved` on the declaring Spec.
properties.title: Feature line

properties.text:
In the blockquote after the H1 (`# M02 — Title`; `M` + digits + optional letter):
- `**Depends on:**` → `DEPENDS_ON` to every milestone linked or named in that segment (`[M02](…) technically (scheduled after [M16](…))` yields M02 and M16). `—` or `nothing` yields none.
- `**Blocks:**` → `DEPENDS_ON` in reverse. Duplicates merge.
- `**Read first:**` → `READS` for every spec reference in the segment, which may span several `>` lines and use `·` or `→` separators. "(whole file)" sets `whole: true`.
- `**Model:**` → `model` (first word: `Opus`, `Sonnet`, `Opusplan`), the rest is kept in `header`.
properties.title: Header lines

properties.text:
The one convention this tool adds:

```markdown
- [ ] **M02.3** Hash and re-parse only changed files (after M02.1)
```

- Regex: `^\s*[-*] \[( |x|X)\] \*\*(M\d+[a-z]?\.\d+)\*\*\s+(.*)`. The ID's milestone part must match the file's milestone, or it is a warning (`task_id_mismatch`).
- `(after M02.1)` or `(after M02.1, M01.4)` at the end yields `BLOCKED_BY`.
- Numbers are never reused within a milestone. A new task takes the next free number, wherever it is inserted.
- **Legacy lines without an ID** get a positional ID `M17.p3` with `stable_id = false` and a `task_unstable_id` warning. `sdd ids --write` rewrites the file once, numbering them after the highest existing number ([SPEC-08 §2](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#2-commands)).
- A task's text includes its continuation lines and nested plain bullets. A nested checkbox is its own task.
- Links and spec references in the task text yield `GOVERNED_BY`; "checks 3–9", "check 6", "checks 1, 3" next to a spec reference yield `VERIFIES` to those AcceptanceChecks.
- The `###` heading above the task becomes `group`.
properties.title: Task IDs

properties.text: *Goal* → `goal`. *Acceptance criteria* → `acceptance` (numbered items). A *Checks finished in later milestones* table is kept as raw text in `header.later_checks`.
properties.title: Other sections

properties.text:
The paragraph starting `**Status:**` or `**Status:` (bold may wrap the whole sentence, as in `**Status: DONE (2026-11-01), with one open item.**`) is `status_text`, with following bullets included.
- `DONE` (case-insensitive) at its start → `status = done`, and `done_date` from `(YYYY-MM-DD)`.
- Otherwise `in_progress` if any task is done or claimed, else `todo`.
- Deviation numbers in the status text (`D021`) link to the deviation with `RAISED_IN` if not already linked.
properties.title: Status

properties.text: `# D012 — Title`, then the bullet fields `**Date / milestone:**` (`2026-10-29 · M04`, optionally followed by the task: `2026-10-29 · M04 · M04.2`), `**Spec:**` (spec references by §2.2, linked or plain), the optional `**Affects:**` (backticked file paths and table names, comma-separated) and `**Status:**`, then the H2 sections *Spec says*, *Implementation does*, *Why*, *Consequences*. Missing sections are warnings, not errors. The task yields `RAISED_IN` → Task (besides the milestone); each `Affects` entry yields `AFFECTS` to the File or Table it names, or goes to `unresolved` (File nodes for code exist from M04a, Table nodes from M04b). Both fields are optional, so the reference formats, which lack them, parse without warnings.
properties.title: Deviation files

properties.text: `DEVIATIONS.md` is parsed only to cross-check: a file without an index row, or a row without a file, is a `deviation_index_mismatch` warning. The index is also where write-back inserts rows ([SPEC-04 §5](SPEC-04-sync.md#5-write-back)).
properties.title: Deviation index

properties.text: CLAUDE.md files, IDEA, design system, HANDOFF and README become Doc nodes with their links as `LINKS_TO`. Plan files (`M20f-plan.md`) become Docs with `kind = plan` and `PLANS` → the milestone.
properties.title: Docs

properties.text:
In `schema_specs` only. A **table section** is a heading whose title, after removing its number and any trailing parenthetical (`(append-only)`, `([SPEC-18](…))`), is one identifier, optionally backticked. It must be followed, before the next heading **of any level**, by a Markdown table whose first header cell is `Column` (a table inside a code fence does not count). Both reference layouts qualify:

```markdown
## 2. `documents`                    ### attachments
| Column | Type | Rules |          | Column | Type | Notes |
```

The header cells are matched by name (case-insensitive): `Column`, `Type`, and `Rules` or `Notes` (the third column when neither exists). Per row: `name` from the first cell (backticks stripped; `created_at`, `updated_at` in one cell yield two columns, and a repeated name keeps the first); `type` from the Type cell without the words `null` / `not null` (`text not null` gives `text`); `notes` from the Rules/Notes cell. From the Type and Rules/Notes cells:
- `not null` → `nullable = false`; otherwise `null` as a word → `true`; otherwise unknown (`null`).
- `PK` → `pk = true`.
- `→ name` or `FK → name` → `REFERENCES` that table (unresolved if it is not defined).

Yields Table, Column, `DEFINES_TABLE` from the section, `HAS_COLUMN`, `REFERENCES`.

properties.title: Sync

properties.text:
- `SDD_WATCH` = `poll` | `native` | `auto` (default). `auto` uses polling when `/.dockerenv` exists, else native events. **Polling is required in Docker on Windows**: inotify sees none of the host's edits through a bind mount; polling sees all of them (verified 2026-11-21).
- Two poll intervals, because every poll stats every watched file and stats through a Windows bind mount are slow: `SDD_POLL_INTERVAL` (default 1 s) for the SDD document globs ([SPEC-03 §1](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#1-rules-and-configuration)), and `SDD_POLL_CODE_INTERVAL` (default 10 s, a minimum) for the rest of the tree. **Measured in M02 (task M02.8, 2026-11-22, `scripts/measure_poll.py` inside the dev container, tree in the bind mount):** one code poll of 20 000 files in 200 folders took **26.6 s (min) / 30.1 s (median)** of 5 runs, about 1.5 ms per file; one SDD poll of this repo took 38.5 ms (min) / 39.1 ms (median). So `SDD_POLL_INTERVAL` stays **1 s**, and the code poll **backs off**: after each poll it waits `max(SDD_POLL_CODE_INTERVAL, 10 × that poll's duration)`, i.e. 10 s on a small tree and about 300 s on a 20 000-file tree through the mount (at most ~10% of a core). The two polls run on separate threads, so a slow code poll never delays an SDD edit (the tests use 0.1 s for both). Native mode watches everything with one observer.
- **What each poll does** (poll mode keeps one snapshot of `(mtime, size)` per path). The **SDD poll** stats every known SDD file and lists the *glob base directories*, the literal folder prefix of each SDD document glob in `paths` (`docs/milestones/` for `docs/milestones/**/M*.md`, `docs/specs/` for `docs/specs/SPEC-*.md`, the project root for `HANDOFF.md`), to find new files without walking the tree. A base followed by `**` is walked recursively, any other base is listed one level, and a glob whose base is the project root (`**/CLAUDE.md`) only lists the root folder. Nested matches such as `src/x/CLAUDE.md` are therefore found by the **code poll**, which walks the whole tree (pruned by the ignore rule below) and also keeps the snapshot current. A file that vanishes mid-poll counts as deleted.
- Detection is one thread; batches are handled on one dedicated thread, so they never overlap. An error in a batch is logged (path count only) and the watcher keeps running.
- Events are debounced for 300 ms and processed as one **batch**.
- Ignored: `.sdd/`, `.git/` (the git poller covers it) and every path the code walker ignores ([§4](#4-code-walker)). Both polls and the native handler share the walker's ignore rules; **the code poll re-reads every ignore file on each poll**, so a `.gitignore` edit takes effect on the next code poll (a path that became ignored leaves the snapshot and is reported as deleted).
properties.title: Watcher

properties.text:
The per-file state is `File.content_hash`: every tracked file, Markdown included, has a File node (SDD documents from M01b, code files from M04a, [SPEC-02 §7](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#7-label--milestone-map)).

The **initial sync** is any sync that runs while `Meta.last_full_sync` is unset (a new or reset store). It records state but emits no Events and sets no `changed_at` or `done_at`: history from before the tool existed is unknown, and a flood of "changes" would bury real ones in `what_changed`.

1. For each changed path, hash it. Equal to the stored hash → skip (this is also how write-back avoids loops, [§5.4](#54-loop-prevention)).
2. Classify: spec, milestone, plan, deviation, deviation index, doc, test file, other.
3. **If the set of SDD document IDs changed** (a spec, milestone or deviation was added, removed or renamed), re-parse **all** SDD Markdown, so links that were unresolved can resolve. Otherwise only changed files are re-parsed. Parsing a few hundred files takes well under a second, so this stays simple and correct.
4. **Phase 1, nodes:** for each parsed file (specs → milestones → plans → deviations → docs), one transaction upserts its nodes by `id`, following the property rules below and in [§2.1](#21-task-upsert-rules). Folder and File nodes for changed code files are upserted in this phase too, so Markdown can link to them (`MENTIONS`, `AFFECTS`).
5. **Phase 2, relationships:** for each parsed file, one transaction deletes the relationships it owns (`src = path`, [SPEC-02 §4](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#4-relationships)) and creates the new ones. Because every node of the batch already exists, links between files of the same batch resolve regardless of order (a spec linking to another spec, `Blocks:` pointing at a later milestone). Targets still missing go to `unresolved`.
6. Then the walker's relationships: `CONTAINS`, feature glob re-expansion, `TESTS` scan of changed test files.
7. After the initial sync: a Section whose `content_hash` changed, or a new Section in a spec that already existed, gets `changed_at = now` and a `section_changed` Event. A new spec gets `spec_added` (its sections keep `changed_at = null`); a removed one gets `spec_removed`.
8. After the batch: `checkpoint()`, update `Meta.last_full_sync` for full scans, and publish one SSE `graph_changed` event listing the changed IDs ([SPEC-07 §3](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md#3-live-events)).

> **DEVIATION:** see [D003](../deviations/D003-relink-on-catalog-change.md) — step 3 re-links every file when anything links resolve against changes (IDs, anchors, title slugs, document paths), not only when the set of document IDs changes

**Startup** runs a full scan through the same path, as one batch: every file's hash against the graph, removed files deleted, then git sync.
properties.title: Incremental sync

properties.text:
An upsert sets `checked`, `title`, `group`, `order` and `stable_id` from Markdown and then recomputes the derived `status` ([SPEC-02 §2](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#task)). The graph-only properties (`claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, `completed_by`, `done_at`, `notes`) change **only** in these cases:

| Case | Effect |
|---|---|
| New task (any sync) | Graph-only properties empty; no Event, even if it is already ticked |
| `checked` unchanged | Graph-only properties untouched |
| Ticked by hand (`false` → `true`), after the initial sync | `done_at = now` if empty; the claim is cleared (`claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, the `CLAIMED` relationship); a `task_completed` Event with `actor = human` |
| Unticked by hand (`true` → `false`) | `done_at` and `completed_by` cleared; `notes` kept (the Events keep the history) |
| The tick written by a tool's own write-back | Handled by that write job: the re-parse in [§5.4](#54-loop-prevention) sees no hand transition, and the Event names the agent, not `human` |

With `writeback = false`, `complete_task` sets `completed_by` and `done_at` without touching Markdown; the derived status counts that as `done`, so a later sync of the unticked line does not revert it.
properties.title: Task upsert rules

properties.text:
- A removed file: delete its File node and every node whose `source_path` is that file, **unless the same `id` is produced by another file in the same batch**. So moving `M17-file-sharing.md` to `done/` (a delete plus an add) keeps M17, its tasks and their claims; only `path` and `source_path` change.
- Deleting a node uses `DETACH DELETE`, so its relationships go too. Stale data is worse than none, because agents trust it.
- Two files producing the same ID: the first by path wins; the other gets a `duplicate_id` warning.
- A Task deleted while claimed emits `task_released` with `actor = sync`.
properties.title: Deletes and renames

properties.text:
- Walks the project root. It skips paths matched by `.gitignore` files (via `pathspec`), `.sddignore`, and the built-in list: `.git`, `.sdd`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build`, `bin`, `obj`, `.next`, `coverage`, `target` (any path segment). **Only that list is built in: there is no blanket "dot names are skipped" rule**, so `.claude/`, `.github/` and `.gitignore` itself are walked.
- **Ignore files.** Each folder's own `.gitignore` applies to the paths beneath it, relative to that folder; the project root also reads `.sddignore` (gitignore syntax). Negation works within one file; **a deeper file cannot un-ignore what a shallower file ignored**. Ignored folders are not entered. The files are read lazily and cached until the next sync or code poll.
- Creates Folder and File nodes with `CONTAINS`. `language` comes from an extension map (and the names `Dockerfile` and `Makefile`; no match leaves the property absent); `is_test` from the `tests` globs ([SPEC-03 §1](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#1-rules-and-configuration)); `lines` is the newline count (plus one for a last line without a newline) for files under 2 MB with no NUL byte in their first 8 KB, else absent. File contents are never stored.
- **Folders.** `dir:<path>` for every folder on the path of a kept file. There is **no root Folder**: top-level files and folders have no parent. A Folder left with no children is deleted after each sync, repeatedly up the tree.
- **Ownership.** The walker writes a File node for **every** walked file, SDD documents included (`path`, `name`, `language`, `size`, `lines`, `is_test`, `last_synced`), but **never sets `content_hash` on an SDD document**: the indexer sets that hash in phase 2 as the "fully synced" marker, and a hash set earlier would make it skip a changed document. The walker deletes only the File nodes of non-SDD paths; the indexer removes SDD documents. The indexer's own state reads (`read_state`, the link catalog fingerprint) are scoped to SDD documents, so code Files are never "removed" by the Markdown sync.
- **Write only differences.** The runtime keeps a cache of what each File node holds. A full sync reads the stored code layer once and diffs the walk against it; a watcher batch re-reads only its paths and diffs them against the cache. Unchanged files are not written, so re-syncing an unchanged repo writes nothing (check 2).
- A soft cap of 20 000 files (`SDD_MAX_FILES`) logs one warning (counts only) and keeps the first 20 000 by path. It also applies to a batch: when it would push the total over the cap, the union is capped the same way and the evicted paths are deleted.
- **Feature globs** are re-expanded when any file is added or removed, or when a Feature's globs changed, as a diff against the stored `IMPLEMENTED_IN` (`src = 'walker'`): a feature whose file set is unchanged is not written (cheap; a feature with no matches gets a `feature_glob_empty` warning, reported in the sync report of every sync that ran the indexer).
- **Mentions.** When a sync adds or removes a file that an SDD document mentions (a backticked path) or names in `Affects`, that document's relationships are rebuilt (phase 2 only) in the same sync, even though its text is unchanged; a document that mentions a file that did not exist yet gets the `MENTIONS` link the sync the file appears, and loses it when the file goes. A new or removed Table re-links every document (the link catalog, D003).
- **TESTS:** changed test files (files under 2 MB, read as UTF-8 with replacement) are scanned for `spec(\d+)_ac(\d+)` (case-insensitive). Each match links the file to `SPEC-<nn>#ac<n>` when it exists, with the numbers read as integers: `spec5_ac03` and `spec05_ac3` both mean `SPEC-05#ac3`. A full sync scans every test file, and so does any sync that created or deleted an AcceptanceCheck, so a check added later still gets its tests. A file's `TESTS` are rewritten only when the wanted set differs from the stored one; they carry `src = 'walker'`.
- Relate's own `fs-to-graph` extension is evaluated in M04a (open item O8). The default is this walker, because extensions run under a Relate host that would have to own the store, and our daemon already does.
properties.title: Code walker

properties.text: `sdd/sync/writeback.py` is the only module that edits Markdown. Every edit runs **inside the write job** that changes the graph, so the file and the graph change together, serialized with every other write.
properties.title: Write-back

properties.text:
| Trigger | Edit |
|---|---|
| `complete_task` | Find the line with `**<task id>**`; replace `[ ]` with `[x]`. Nothing else on the line changes |
| `log_deviation` | (1) Next number = highest D-number in the files **and** the index, + 1 (computed inside the job, so parallel agents never collide). (2) Write `docs/deviations/D<nnn>-<kebab-title>.md` from the template in `DEVIATIONS.md` (or the built-in one), with the task after the milestone in **Date / milestone:** and the resolved `affects` entries in **Affects:** ([SPEC-03 §5.1](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#51-deviation-files)), so the links are rebuildable. (3) Insert the index row at the **top** of the index table, replacing a `*(none yet)*` placeholder row. (4) Append `> **DEVIATION:** see [D<nnn>](…) — <summary>` as the last line of each amended section's own body (before its first child heading), preceded by a blank line so it never joins a table, list or paragraph above it. When the whole spec is amended, the note goes at the end of the header blockquote, as its own `>` line |
| `complete_milestone` | Replace the `**Status:**` paragraph with `**Status:** DONE (<date>). <verification> Deviations: <list or none>.`; move the file (and its plan file) to `done/` if that folder exists, and **rewrite every relative link to the moved files** in the SDD documents (path part only; text and anchor unchanged), and re-base the moved files' own relative links on their new folder, in the same job |
| `sdd export --claude-status` | Replace the text between `<!-- sdd:status -->` and `<!-- /sdd:status -->` in CLAUDE.md; nothing outside the markers |
properties.title: Edits

properties.text:
- Writes are atomic: write a temp file in the same folder, then rename. Line endings (LF or CRLF), the final newline and UTF-8 encoding are preserved.
- Before editing, the file is re-read and the target re-located by ID or heading, never by a cached line number. If the target is gone (a human edited it away), the job fails with `source_changed` and the graph is not changed.
- **Order inside a job:** check → change the graph (uncommitted) → write the Markdown files (atomic renames) → re-parse them ([§5.4](#54-loop-prevention)) → `commit()`. Markdown goes last because it cannot be rolled back. If the commit still fails after the files were written, Markdown is ahead of the graph; the watcher's next batch reconciles it, since Markdown is the source of truth.
- **Edits are idempotent**, because a retried job runs again ([SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)): a box already `[x]` is left alone, a deviation file or index row that already exists for this job is reused, a status line already `DONE` is not written twice.
- The daemon **never commits** to git. People and agents commit.
- `writeback = false` in config turns write-back off. `complete_task` still works and completion lives only in the graph ([§2.1](#21-task-upsert-rules)); `sdd status` says so. `log_deviation` and `complete_milestone` fail with `writeback_disabled`, because a deviation or a DONE status that exists only in the graph would contradict the Markdown.

properties.text: Defined once, in [SPEC-02 §2](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#graph-only-state-canonical-list). A full rebuild (`sdd sync --reset`) drops it; a normal sync keeps it.

properties.text: After writing a file, the same job re-parses it and stores its new `content_hash`. When the watcher then reports the change, the hash matches and nothing happens. For a move, the job also deletes the old path's File node and updates `path` / `source_path` on the moved nodes itself, rather than leaving it to a later delete-plus-add batch.
properties.title: Loop prevention

properties.text:
- On startup, and when `git rev-parse HEAD` changes (polled every 3 s, which works through bind mounts). No git binary, not a repository, no commit yet, or a project that is a sub-folder of a larger repository: git sync is skipped (`git` is `null` in the sync result), never an error. Every git call is `git -c core.quotepath=off --no-optional-locks -C <root> …` with a 30 s timeout and no terminal prompt.
- New commits: `git log --reverse -n <max> --name-status --format=%x1e%H%x1f%P%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%s <last>..HEAD` (records split on `\x1e`, fields on `\x1f`). **`author` is the name only, never the email** (the graph can be public). `at` is the author date in UTC (`…Z`). `message` is the subject. Name-status letters `A`, `M`, `D` are kept; `R*` is `R` (the new path is linked, both paths go into `paths`), `C*` is `A`, `T` is `M`. Merge commits list no files. The first sync is limited to the newest `SDD_GIT_MAX_COMMITS` (default 2000). `Meta.last_git_sha` is stored after each sync.
- **History rewritten** (`last_git_sha` is not an ancestor of HEAD: rebase, reset, branch switch): delete Commit nodes no longer reachable within the limit (`git rev-list -n <max> HEAD`), with every relationship whose `src` is `git:<that sha>` (`TOUCHES` is Task to File, so detaching the Commit does not remove it), and add the new ones. **The deletes run in their own write job, before the job that adds commits**: the engine panics when one transaction deletes a relationship it created. Relationships with `src = "tool"` are never touched.
- **The code step runs first.** The new commits' paths that exist, are not ignored and are not known to the code walker yet go through it before linking, so `CHANGED` and `TOUCHES` find the File nodes of files created in the same commit (the code poll alone waits at least 10 s, and a commit must show its links within 3 s).
- Per commit (written in jobs of about 200 commits, oldest first; the last job stores `Meta.last_git_sha`): Commit node, `PARENT` to parents already in the graph, `CHANGED {change}` to files that still exist (all paths stay in `Commit.paths`), `COMPLETES` for each `[M02.3]`, `PART_OF` for `(M20f)` (or a bare `M20f`) when no task ID is present. Then `TOUCHES` from each completed task to the commit's changed files. Every relationship gets `src = "git:<sha>"`. **A Task or Milestone that does not exist at sync time gets no link and no `unresolved` entry.** Commits create no Events.
- A commit never changes a task's status. Markdown stays the source of truth; a `COMPLETES` link on an unticked task is shown as a warning in `sdd status`.
- Docker: the image sets `git config --global --add safe.directory '*'`, because the bind-mounted repo is owned by another user.
properties.title: Git sync

properties.text:
1. With `SDD_WATCH=poll`, editing a spec section on the host updates that Section's `text` and `changed_at` within 3 s, and no other Section's `changed_at`.
2. Re-syncing an unchanged repo writes nothing (no `changed_at` moves, no Events).
3. Moving a milestone file to `done/` keeps its ID, its tasks and an active claim; only `path` changes.
4. Deleting a spec file removes its Spec, Sections and checks, and the READS/GOVERNED_BY relationships pointing at them; the referring milestones list the links as `unresolved`.
5. Adding a spec that an existing milestone already links to resolves that link in the same batch.
6. `complete_task` ticks exactly one line, preserving CRLF line endings, and the watcher does not trigger a second sync of that file.
7. Two concurrent `log_deviation` calls produce D-numbers n and n+1, two files, two index rows at the top and two spec notes.
8. A `.gitignore`d path and `node_modules/` produce no File nodes.
9. A commit `feat: walker [M04.2]` yields COMPLETES to M04.2 and TOUCHES to its changed files; a later `git reset --hard HEAD~1` removes that Commit node.
10. Editing a task line by hand between a claim and `complete_task` (ID kept) still ticks the right line; removing the line makes `complete_task` fail with `source_changed`.
11. The initial sync of a fresh store resolves links between files of the same batch whatever the order (a spec linking to a later spec, a `Blocks:` link to a later milestone), and records zero Events and no `changed_at` / `done_at`; a pre-ticked task is `done` with `done_at = null`.
12. `complete_milestone` on a milestone that another milestone links to moves the file to `done/`, rewrites that link, and the next sync shows zero unresolved links and zero `link_moved` warnings.
13. Hand-ticking a claimed task clears the claim; with `writeback = false`, a `complete_task` stays `done` after the file is re-synced.

properties.title: Agent tools (MCP)

properties.text:
1. Tools validate input, call one `service/` function, and return JSON. Every tool's result is also what the matching HTTP endpoint ([SPEC-07](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md)) and CLI command return.
2. **Every tool takes `agent`** (a free name such as `opus-orch`, `sonnet-2`): required on write tools, optional on read tools. Claude Code subagents share their parent's MCP connection, so identity cannot come from the connection. Any tool call with `agent` updates `Agent.last_seen`, which is how the daemon knows an agent is alive ([§3](#3-claims)). Agents keep the **same name across sessions** (the orchestrator is `opus-orch`), so `what_changed` and claims follow them.
3. Writes run as one job in the write queue: check, change the graph, write back Markdown, emit an Event, all or nothing.
4. Results are compact: IDs, titles and text, never whole files. Every result carries `synced_at` (the last sync time) so an agent can tell if context may be stale.

properties.title: Tool index

properties.text:
- **Claimable** = `status = todo`, no live claim, every `BLOCKED_BY` task `done`, and every `DEPENDS_ON` milestone `done`.
- `next_tasks` returns claimable tasks ordered by milestone `order`, then task `order`. Each item: `id`, `title`, `milestone_id`, `group`, `governed_by` (IDs), and `overlaps`: tasks claimed right now that share a governing section or a mentioned file, as a hint that running them in parallel may conflict.
- `claim_task` checks and sets in **one write job**, so of two simultaneous claims exactly one wins. Re-claiming your own task succeeds (idempotent).
- **Stale claims** ([DEC-003](../decisions/DEC-003-claim-liveness.md)): a claim is stale when the claiming agent's `last_seen` is older than `SDD_CLAIM_TTL` (default **2 h**, long enough that a working agent, which may go quiet during a long build or test run, never looks dead). A claim on a stale task succeeds and emits `task_released` (actor `sync`) before `task_claimed`. There is no heartbeat tool: an agent blocked in one long command could not call it anyway.
- **Forced release:** `release_task(task_id, agent, force=true)` frees a claim held by someone else, for when the orchestrator or a human knows the holder has died and should not wait for the TTL. It emits `task_released` with `actor` = the claim holder and `data.forced_by` = the caller. Without `force`, `complete_task` and `release_task` require the caller to hold the claim (`not_claimed_by_you`).
- A task ticked by hand in Markdown is done whoever held it; the claim is cleared.
properties.title: Claims

properties.text:
The minimum an agent needs to build one task, so it does not read whole files.

```json
{
  "task": {"id": "M02.3", "title": "…", "group": "Sync", "status": "claimed", "blocked_by": []},
  "milestone": {"id": "M02", "title": "…", "goal": "…", "acceptance": ["…"], "model": "Opusplan"},
  "sections": [{"id": "SPEC-04#2", "title": "Incremental sync", "text": "…", "why": "governs task",
                "amended_by": ["D004"]}],
  "outline": [{"id": "SPEC-04#5", "title": "Write-back", "why": "milestone reads", "chars": 3120}],
  "checks": [{"id": "SPEC-04#ac2", "text": "…"}],
  "deviations": [{"id": "D004", "title": "…", "status": "open", "implementation_does": "…", "amends": ["SPEC-04#2"]}],
  "upstream": [{"id": "M02.1", "title": "…", "notes": "…", "files_touched": ["src/sdd/sync/watcher.py"]}],
  "code": {"features": ["sync"], "files": ["src/sdd/sync/indexer.py"], "tables": [],
           "recent_commits": [{"short": "a1b2c3d", "message": "…"}]},
  "size": {"chars": 9120, "tokens_est": 2280, "truncated": []},
  "synced_at": "2026-11-25T03:12:00Z"
}
```

Every section named below is included **with its descendants** ([SPEC-03 §2.2](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#22-spec-reference-grammar)): `SPEC-00#6` brings §6.1–6.7 along. Each descendant is its own item in `sections` (so `amended_by` stays per section), in document order, with `why` naming the reference that pulled it in.

What goes where, with `detail = "task"` (default):
1. **`sections` (full text):** the task's `GOVERNED_BY` sections (a governing Spec brings its top-level sections); the *Acceptance checks* section of each spec its `VERIFIES` checks belong to; every section in `always_include` (`.sdd/config.toml`, a list of references, default `["SPEC-00 §6"]`, skipped when it does not resolve). If the task governs nothing, the milestone's `READS` sections are used instead, and stand in for governing sections everywhere below (they are never dropped, and their specs give `code` its features).
2. **`outline`:** the milestone's other `READS` targets as `id`, `title`, `chars`. A `whole: true` spec appears as its section list. The agent fetches what it needs with `read_section`.
3. **`deviations`:** every deviation that `AMENDS` an included section. Open ones carry `implementation_does`; resolved ones carry the title only, since the spec already says it.
4. **`upstream`:** `BLOCKED_BY` tasks and done tasks of the same milestone, with completion notes and files touched from their Events.
5. **`code`:** features of the governing specs, their files (max 50 paths), tables mentioned by the task or its sections, and the 5 latest commits touching those files.

`detail = "milestone"` puts every `READS` section in `sections` (the Markdown-equivalent view, used by the benchmark). Above `max_chars`, parts are dropped in this order (code, upstream, outline, then the longest non-governing sections) and listed in `truncated`. Spec text is never cut mid-section.
properties.title: get_context

properties.text:
- `amends`: one or more spec references (grammar in [SPEC-03 §2.2](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#22-spec-reference-grammar)), at least one, each must resolve (`unknown_section`).
- Creates the file, index row and spec notes ([SPEC-04 §5.1](SPEC-04-sync.md#51-edits)), the Deviation node with `RAISED_IN` the task and its milestone, `AMENDS`, and `AFFECTS` for `affects` entries that resolve to a File or Table (an entry that resolves to neither is `invalid_input`). The task and the affects list are written into the file, so these links are owned by it (`src` = its path) and survive a rebuild.
- Returns `{id, path}`. Every agent whose current claim's context includes an amended section sees the deviation on its next `get_context` or `what_changed`.

> **DEVIATION:** see [D004](../deviations/D004-affects-may-name-project-files-that-have-no-file-node-yet.md) — Affects may name project files that have no File node yet
properties.title: log_deviation

properties.text: Fails with `milestone_incomplete` (listing the open tasks) unless every task is done. Writes the status line with today's date, the given verification text and the deviations `RAISED_IN` the milestone (or "Deviations: none"); moves the file per [SPEC-04 §5.1](SPEC-04-sync.md#51-edits); emits `milestone_done`.
properties.title: complete_milestone

properties.text:
`since` is an ISO time, an event ID, or `"last_session"` (needs `agent`). **`"last_session"` means "since this agent last called `what_changed`"** ([DEC-003](../decisions/DEC-003-claim-liveness.md)): every call stores `Agent.last_changes_at`, and the next `last_session` call returns everything after the previous value. No session boundaries are guessed. An agent's first call returns the last 24 h with `first_session: true`. Returns grouped lists: `sections_changed` (id, title, changed_at), `specs_added`, `specs_removed`, `deviations` (logged or status changed), `tasks_completed`, `tasks_claimed`, `milestones_done`, each item with actor and time. This replaces re-reading files to see what moved.

> **DEVIATION:** see [D005](../deviations/D005-what-changed-bounds-are-inclusive.md) — what_changed bounds are inclusive

properties.text:
- `sdd init` writes `.mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers": {"sdd": {"type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:8770/mcp"}}}` (plus `"headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${SDD_TOKEN}"}` when `SDD_TOKEN` is set: Claude Code expands the variable from the environment, so the token itself is never written to a file). An existing `.mcp.json` is **merged**: the `sdd` entry is added and other servers are kept; only an existing `sdd` entry needs `--force` to replace.
- It also writes `.claude/skills/sdd/SKILL.md` with the **agent protocol**, and offers a CLAUDE.md snippet:
  - **Orchestrator:** `status` → `next_tasks` → launch one subagent per task that has no `overlaps`, telling each its agent name and task ID → review returned work; if a subagent failed, `release_task(…, force=true)` its task → `complete_milestone` when the acceptance criteria are verified.
  - **Worker:** `claim_task` → `get_context` → `read_section` for anything in `outline` it needs → build and test → `log_deviation` for every intentional departure → `complete_task` with notes, files and commit → report.
  - **Any session start:** `what_changed(since="last_session", agent=<own name>)` instead of re-reading docs.
- The server's MCP `instructions` field carries a three-line version of the protocol.

4. A claim whose agent has not been seen for longer than the TTL can be claimed by another agent, and a `task_released` event is recorded.
5. `get_context` for a task with a governing section amended by an open deviation includes that section's full text and the deviation's `implementation_does`.

7. `complete_task` ticks the line, records notes and files in the event, and returns the tasks it unblocked.
8. `complete_milestone` with an open task fails with `milestone_incomplete`; with all done, it writes the status line listing the milestone's deviations.
9. `what_changed(since="last_session", agent=A)` returns a section edited by a human after A's previous `what_changed` call, and not one edited before it; A's first call ever returns the last 24 h with `first_session: true`.
10. `read_section("SPEC-02 §3–4")` returns two sections.
