properties.text:
1. These are the queries that need a graph: multi-hop, mixed-type and explained. **Every returned item carries `via`**, the chain of relationships that connects it to the target, so a person or agent can see why it is there.
2. Traversals are fixed per target kind (no free path expansion), bounded by `depth` (default 3, 1 to 5) and by 50 items per group (`counts` gives the full numbers, for every group). **Depth counts hops**: the relationships in an item's `via` chain, **not counting containment** (`HAS_SECTION`, `HAS_CHECK`, `HAS_COLUMN`), so a section's spec is one `<-HAS_SECTION` step even when the section is nested, and a table's columns are at 0 hops. A node reached by several chains keeps the one with the fewest hops (a tie keeps the first in traversal order, where `AFFECTS` comes before `MENTIONS`); the target itself is never an item.
3. Every traversal is a named query in `src/sdd/graph/queries/*.cypher`, loaded by `graph/queries.py` ([SPEC-01 §2](SPEC-01-architecture.md#2-repo-layout)), so the static demo can run the same files ([SPEC-11 §6](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#6-static-demo-github-pages)). `service/impact.py` calls them by name and assembles groups and `via` chains; it holds no Cypher of its own. Results are sorted by group, then by relevance (fewer hops first), then by ID.
properties.title: Rules

properties.text:
`impact(target, depth=3)`: if this changes, what else is affected?

**Target resolution** (after `ids.normalise`), in two steps:
1. **Unambiguous forms** resolve directly, by their format: a spec reference → Section or Spec; a task, milestone or deviation ID; a prefixed ID (`table:x`, `column:t.c`, `file:p`, `feature:s`, `domain:s`).
2. **Bare names** are looked up in every kind at once: table name, `table.column`, existing file path, feature name or slug, section title slug. Exactly one match resolves. More than one (a table and a feature both called `attachments`; a column name shared by two tables) returns `ambiguous_target` with the candidates as prefixed IDs (section IDs for sections), sorted, so the caller can repeat with one of them. None is `node_not_found`. Matching is exact except that feature names compare case-insensitively and a section matches by `id_slug` of its title; a bare column name matches any table's column, and a section that defines a table is not a candidate (it is that table), so `documents` is the table.

**Traversals:**

| Target | Follows |
|---|---|
| Table | its Columns · Columns elsewhere that `REFERENCES` it (dependent tables) · the defining Section and its Spec · Sections, Tasks and Deviations that `MENTIONS` it or `LINKS_TO` the defining section · Features that `USES_TABLE` it → their Files and Specs · Tasks `GOVERNED_BY` those sections · Commits that `COMPLETES` those Tasks (so the centrepiece table reaches every group) · Deviations that `AMENDS` those sections or `AFFECTS` the table · Tests of the defining spec's checks |
| Column | as Table, starting from its table, plus Columns that reference the same table |
| Section | child Sections · Sections that `LINKS_TO` it · Milestones that `READS` it · Tasks `GOVERNED_BY` it, open and done · Deviations that `AMENDS` it · Tables it defines or mentions · Features of its Spec → Files · Checks of its Spec → test Files |
| Spec | as Section, for every section of the spec |
| File | Features `IMPLEMENTED_IN` it → their Specs · Sections and Tasks that `MENTIONS` it · Tasks that `TOUCHES` it · the 10 latest Commits that `CHANGED` it → the Tasks they `COMPLETES` · Deviations that `AFFECTS` it or amend its features' specs · Checks it `TESTS` |
| Feature | its Files, Tables, Specs, Domain, and the Section traversal over its Specs |
| Task | its Milestone · the Sections and Specs it is `GOVERNED_BY` · Tasks it is `BLOCKED_BY` and Tasks blocked by it · Files it `TOUCHES` · Commits that `COMPLETES` it · Deviations `RAISED_IN` it |
| Milestone | its Tasks (open and done) · what it `READS` · Milestones it `DEPENDS_ON` and Milestones that depend on it · Deviations `RAISED_IN` it · Commits `PART_OF` it |
| Domain | its Features (`BELONGS_TO`) |
| Deviation | what it `AMENDS` · what it `AFFECTS` · the Milestone and Task it is `RAISED_IN` |

Any other node an unambiguous ID names (a Commit, an AcceptanceCheck, a Folder, a Doc) resolves, but has no traversal: its groups are empty.

**Output:**

```json
{
  "target": {"id": "table:attachments", "label": "Table", "title": "attachments"},
  "groups": {
    "specs": [], "sections": [], "milestones": [], "tables": [], "features": [], "files": [],
    "tasks_open": [], "tasks_done": [], "deviations": [], "tests": [], "commits": []
  },
  "counts": {"specs": 0, "sections": 0, "milestones": 0, "tables": 0, "features": 0, "files": 37, "tasks_open": 0, "tasks_done": 0, "deviations": 0, "tests": 0, "commits": 0},
  "synced_at": "…"
}
```

Every group is always present, sorted by hops then ID. Placement: Columns go in `tables`; Domains in `features`; AcceptanceChecks, and test Files reached through `TESTS`, in `tests`; Tasks by `status` into `tasks_done` or `tasks_open`. `milestones` holds the Milestones the Section traversal returns. Each item: `{id, label, title, via: ["table:attachments", "<-DEFINES_TABLE", "SPEC-02#attachments", "<-LINKS_TO", "SPEC-18#2"]}`. `via` uses `->TYPE` and `<-TYPE` for direction, read from the target outward. Tasks and Deviations also carry `status`.

properties.text:
`find_code(feature?, domain?, table?, spec?, text?)`: at least one argument; several are intersected.
- `feature` / `domain`: Files via `IMPLEMENTED_IN` (domain through its features).
- `table`: Files of features that use it, plus the Files named (`MENTIONS`, or `AFFECTS` by a deviation that also affects the table) by the Sections, Tasks and Deviations that mention the table, plus files whose path has a `migrations` or `models` segment and contains the table name (case-insensitive; its `via` ends `~PATH`).
- `spec`: Files of the spec's features, plus Files that `MENTIONS`-linked sections name.
- `text`: case-insensitive substring of `File.path` (a plain `CONTAINS`; the full-text index needs `CALL`, which the named queries avoid).

Each given argument yields files with the `via` of their first route; the result is the intersection, with the `via` of the first argument in the order feature, domain, table, spec, text. Returns `{files: [{path, language, via}] (sorted by path, at most 50), counts: {files}, synced_at}`.

properties.text:
Named queries used by the dashboard, `sdd export --mermaid <preset>` and the README:

| Preset | Shows |
|---|---|
| `schema` | Labels and relationship types with counts (the meta-graph): one node per label (`{id: <label>, label: "Label", title: "Table (12)", props: {count}}`) and one edge per (from label, type, to label) with a `count` field |
| `milestone:<id>` | The milestone, its tasks, READS sections, and deviations raised in it |
| `impact:<target>` | The `impact` result as a graph |
| `explain:<path>` | The `explain` result as a graph |
| `lineage:<section>` | Deviations amending the section → the tasks they were raised in → the files those tasks touched |
| `feature:<slug>` | Feature → specs, files, tables |

`presets()` lists them as `[{name, params, description}]` (`name` is the pattern above, `params` the placeholder names). A preset's graph has the `/api/graph` shape `{nodes: [{id, label, title, props}], edges: [{source, target, type}]}`, built from the `via` chains: a step `(a, '<-T', b)` is the edge `b -T-> a`, `(a, '->T', b)` is `a -T-> b`. An unknown preset or target is `node_not_found`.

properties.text:
1. Starlette routes in `web/api.py` validate, call one `service/` function, and return its JSON. Same results as the MCP tools.
2. Errors use the one shape ([SPEC-00 §6.4](SPEC-00-overview.md#64-errors)) with the codes of [SPEC-05 §8](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#8-error-codes) and these HTTP statuses: 400 (`invalid_input`, `query_rejected`, `ambiguous_target`), 401 (`unauthorized`), 403 (`read_only`, `forbidden_origin`, `forbidden_host`, `writeback_disabled`), 404 (`*_not_found`, `unknown_section`), 409 (`already_claimed`, `task_done`, `task_blocked`, `not_claimed_by_you`, `milestone_incomplete`, `source_changed`, `daemon_running`), 429 (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`), 503 (`write_conflict`, `query_timeout`). A code without a status here is a bug.
3. **IDs and references in URLs are percent-encoded** (`encodeURIComponent`), because they contain `#`, `/`, `:`, spaces and `§`: `GET /api/nodes/SPEC-02%232`, `GET /api/nodes/file%3Asrc%2Fsdd%2Fcli.py`, `GET /api/sections/SPEC-03%20%C2%A74.2`. Path parameters that hold an ID use Starlette's `{id:path}` converter. The dashboard's URL hash encodes the same way (`#impact/table%3Aattachments`).
4. Read endpoints that mirror an MCP tool accept that tool's optional `agent` as a query parameter; write endpoints take `agent` in the JSON body (SPEC-05 §1 rule 2).
5. The dashboard is plain static HTML + ES modules + vendored Cytoscape.js. **No build step, no framework.** The same files run in the daemon, in `sdd public`, and on GitHub Pages ([SPEC-11 §6](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#6-static-demo-github-pages)) through a data adapter (`api.js`: HTTP, or the in-browser WASM store). The adapter adds the bearer header when the daemon has a token ([SPEC-09 §2](SPEC-09-security.md#2-local-daemon) rule 2).

properties.text: `GET /api/events` (SSE, keep-alive comment every 15 s). Event types: `task` (`{id, status, claimed_by, milestone_id}`), `deviation` (`{id, title}`), `graph_changed` (`{ids: [...], kinds: [...]}`), `milestone` (`{id, status}`). properties.text:
One page, five tabs; the URL hash keeps the tab and selection (`#impact/table%3Aattachments`, encoded per [§1](#1-rules) rule 3) so README links can deep-link.

1. **Board** (default): milestone picker; columns *To do · In progress · Done*; cards show ID, title, group, and the claiming agent as a coloured chip. Cards move live with a short highlight. Header: counts and the last few events as a ticker. **This is the demo video's main shot.**
2. **Graph:** Cytoscape view with a label filter (checkboxes, colour per label), search box (ID or title), click to show properties in a side panel, double-click to expand neighbours, *Reset*. Opens on the `schema` preset or on a milestone.
3. **Impact:** a target box with autocomplete (tables, sections, files, features). Shows the result as grouped lists **and** as a graph where the target is centred and the `via` chains are drawn; clicking an item shows its chain.
4. **Explain:** a file picker (searchable tree). Shows the summary paragraph and the chain feature → spec → tasks/commits → deviations as a left-to-right layered graph.
5. **Query:** a Cypher box with example queries (the presets as Cypher), a results table, and *Show as graph* when the result has nodes. In public mode with `SDD_PUBLIC_QUERY=presets`, the box is read-only and only presets run.

Look: system font stack, light and dark themes via `prefers-color-scheme` and a toggle, colour tokens as CSS custom properties, one accent colour per label, sentence case, no emoji. Layout works from 360 px wide (tabs collapse into a select).

properties.title: CLI and exports

properties.text:
1. `sdd` is a Typer app. Commands call the daemon API when a daemon runs for the project ([SPEC-01 §1](SPEC-01-architecture.md#1-process-model) rule 3), otherwise `service/` directly on a read-only snapshot (reads) or the store (writes). Exports and `snapshot` read the store files directly, daemon or not: a `read_only` open works beside a running writer (O12) and there is no endpoint for a full dump.
2. Every command takes `--project PATH` (default: walk up from the current folder to the first folder containing `.sdd/` or `docs/specs/`), `--store PATH` (default `<project>/.sdd/graph`; `:memory:` parses into a throwaway in-memory store and writes nothing, which is how `sdd doctor` and `sdd status` run against a read-only checkout such as the reference projects) and `--json` (the result or error as JSON). Human output is plain text tables, no colour when not a TTY.
3. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 any other error, 2 usage (`invalid_input`, `ambiguous_target`), 3 not found (`*_not_found`, `unknown_section`), 4 conflict (the 409 codes of [SPEC-07 §1](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md#1-rules), and `daemon_running`), 5 `write_conflict`.
4. Write commands that edit Markdown or open the store writable (`sync`, `ids --write`) refuse with `daemon_running` while a daemon runs; the coordination commands (`claim`, `done`, …) go through its API instead.
properties.title: Rules

properties.text:
| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `sdd init` | Create `.sdd/config.toml` (detected paths), `.sdd/.gitignore` (locks, `daemon.json`), `.mcp.json`, `.claude/skills/sdd/SKILL.md`; print the CLAUDE.md snippet ([SPEC-05 §9](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#9-claude-code-integration)). Never overwrites without `--force`; an existing `.mcp.json` gets the `sdd` server merged in |
| `sdd --version` | Print the `sdd` and `relate-db` versions |
| `sdd info` | Project root, store path, whether a daemon runs (and its port), node and relationship counts per label and type, schema version |
| `sdd daemon [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8770]` | Run the daemon ([SPEC-01 §5](SPEC-01-architecture.md#5-daemon-lifecycle)) |
| `sdd public --store PATH [--port 8780]` | Run the read-only public server ([SPEC-09 §4](SPEC-09-security.md#4-public-mode)) |
| `sdd sync [--reset]` | One full sync without a daemon (code walker, Markdown, git; [SPEC-04 §2, §4, §6](SPEC-04-sync.md)); `--reset` empties the store first, in place (graph-only state is lost; asks unless `--yes`; `--json` needs `--yes`). The `--json` result adds `code` (`added`, `updated`, `removed`, `folders`, `tests_links`, `capped`) and `git` (`added`, `removed`, `head`; `null` when skipped) |
| `sdd status` | Milestones, task counts, claims, warnings, unresolved links, unticked tasks with COMPLETES commits |
| `sdd doctor` | Reads the Markdown only and never opens the store, so it works on a read-only checkout. Every parser warning and unresolved link, deviation index mismatches, duplicate IDs; exit 1 if any `error`. The counts include tables, columns and resolved `REFERENCES` |
| `sdd ids --write [--milestone M17]` | Add stable task IDs to legacy checkbox lines ([SPEC-03 §4.2](SPEC-03-markdown-parsing.md#42-task-ids)); shows a diff and asks unless `--yes` |
| `sdd next [--milestone M] [--limit N] [--agent A]` · `sdd claim T --agent A` · `sdd release T --agent A [--reason …] [--force]` · `sdd done T --agent A [--notes …] [--files PATH]… [--commit SHA]` | The coordination tools for humans and scripts |
| `sdd deviation T --agent A --title … --amends REF… --spec-says … --does … --why … [--consequences …] [--affects …] [--resolved]` · `sdd milestone-done M --agent A --verification TEXT` | `log_deviation` and `complete_milestone` ([SPEC-05 §5–6](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#5-log_deviation)) |
| `sdd context T [--detail milestone]` · `sdd section REF` | Print a context packet or sections |
| `sdd impact TARGET [--depth N]` · `sdd explain PATH` · `sdd find [--feature F] [--domain D] [--table T] [--spec S] [--text X]` · `sdd changes --since X [--agent A]` | [SPEC-06](SPEC-06-code-context.md) and `what_changed`. `impact` prints the target, then every non-empty group (`tables (2)`) with one line per item and its `via` chain, and `… 50 of 120` when a group is capped; `explain` prints the summary, then its groups; `find` prints one `path  (language)` line per file and `N files` (`--json` prints the result as is) |
| `sdd query CYPHER` | Read-only Cypher through the guard |
| `sdd export …` | [§3](#3-exports-and-snapshots) |
| `sdd snapshot [--out DIR]` | Checkpoint and write the committed copies ([§3](#3-exports-and-snapshots)) |
| `sdd bench …` | [SPEC-10 §5](SPEC-10-testing-and-benchmark.md#5-benchmark) |
| `sdd demo prepare --sample DIR --data DIR` | Copy the sample into a fresh working copy and apply its start state ([SPEC-11 §4](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#4-sprint-replay) step 1) |
| `sdd demo replay --sample DIR --data DIR [--seed N]` | Prepare, then run the simulated agents in a loop ([SPEC-11 §4](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#4-sprint-replay)) |
| `sdd demo serve --sample DIR --data DIR [--host] [--port 8770]` | Prepare, then run the daemon on the copy. One command, so the judges' image can keep `ENTRYPOINT ["sdd"]` ([SPEC-11 §2](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#2-compose)) |

> **DEVIATION:** see [D002](../deviations/D002-reset-empties-store-in-place.md) — `sdd sync --reset` empties the store in place instead of deleting its directory
properties.title: Commands

properties.text:
- `sdd export --mermaid PRESET|CYPHER [--out FILE]`: renders a preset ([SPEC-06 §5](SPEC-06-code-context.md#5-presets)) or a query result as a Mermaid `flowchart LR`. GitHub renders the output natively, so the README shows it. Rules, so that output is deterministic (golden files):
  - **Argument:** it is Cypher when it starts with `MATCH`, `OPTIONAL MATCH`, `WITH`, `UNWIND`, `CALL` or `RETURN` (any case), else a preset name. Cypher runs through the query guard ([SPEC-09 §3](SPEC-09-security.md#3-query-guard)); every result value that is a map with an `id` becomes a node, and a row with columns `source` and `target` (IDs or node maps, optional `type`, default `RELATED`) becomes an edge. Unknown IDs are dropped.
  - **Nodes:** the preset's root first, the rest sorted by `(label, id)`, at most 60; edges to dropped nodes go too and the last line is `%% truncated N nodes`. Mermaid IDs are `n0`, `n1`, … in that order. Shapes per label: Spec `[[ ]]`, Section `[ ]`, Task `( )`, Deviation `{{ }}`, File `[/ /]`, Table `[( )]`, Milestone `([ ])`, Feature `> ]`, anything else `[ ]`.
  - **Labels:** `"<id>: <title>"` (just the ID when they are equal; a Commit shows `<short sha>: <message>`; the `schema` preset shows its node title, `Table (12)`), cut to 60 characters with `…`, in double quotes with `"`, `<`, `>` written as `#quot;`, `#lt;`, `#gt;`.
  - **Edges:** `nA -->|TYPE| nB`, sorted by source, type, target; an edge with a `count` reads `|"TYPE (12)"|`.
  - **Classes:** one `classDef <label lowercased>` per label present (the dashboard's hues) and one `class` line per label; the nodes of the `schema` preset take the colour of the label they stand for.

  The `schema` preset renders labels and relationship types with counts.
- `sdd export --cypher [--out FILE]`: the whole graph as an idempotent Cypher script, used by the static demo ([SPEC-11 §6](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#6-static-demo-github-pages)). **One statement per line, each ending in `;`**, so a loader splits on newlines: two `//` header lines (counts, no timestamp, so re-exports diff cleanly), then `MERGE (n:<Label> {id: '<id>'}) SET n += {<props>};` per node sorted by `id`, then `MATCH (a:<L> {id: '…'}), (b:<L> {id: '…'}) MERGE (a)-[r:<TYPE> {<props>}]->(b);` per relationship sorted by source, type, target. Properties are written **as stored** (a map such as `header` stays the `header_json` string, [SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)), keys sorted, nulls skipped. Relationship properties are part of the `MERGE` pattern, because two relationships of one type between the same nodes exist (a deviation's file and the spec note that amends the same section differ in `src`). Strings are single-quoted with backslash, quote, newline and tab escaped; a carriage return and any other unprintable character is written `\uXXXX` (Relate reads `\n` and `\t` but not `\r`). `service/exports.py` has `load_cypher(store, script)`, which runs the lines in one write job.
- `sdd export --json [--out FILE]`: `{nodes, edges}` in the `/api/graph` shape for the whole graph (no limit), nodes sorted by `id`, edges by source, type, target; also for the static demo.
- `sdd export --claude-status`: rewrites the CLAUDE.md block between `<!-- sdd:status -->` and `<!-- /sdd:status -->` ([SPEC-04 §5.1](SPEC-04-sync.md#51-edits)); the marker lines and every byte outside them stay as they are (CRLF files keep CRLF). Without the file or a marker the command fails with `invalid_input` (exit 2) and prints the two lines to add. The block, deterministic and without timestamps, is one generated line and four bullets: `**Done:**` (`M01 Title (date)` for each done milestone, in order), `**Next:**` (the first milestone not done, as a link, its open/total task count and its *Read first* sections), `**Open deviations:**` (`D003 Title (M03b)`), `**Active claims:**` (`M05a.3 by sonnet-1`); `none` where empty. The file is written through `sync/writeback.py` after re-reading it (`source_changed` if it changed meanwhile); a second run writes nothing and reports `changed: false`. Result `{path, changed}`.
- `sdd snapshot [--out .sdd/snapshots]`: writes the committed copies for judges: `graph/` (a consistent copy of the directory store that keeps the `.cypherlite.lock` markers in its root and `wal/`, which a read-only open needs, and drops `.cypherlite.writer`; O11, [D001](../deviations/D001-store-copies-keep-lock-markers.md)), `graph.rl` (single file) and `graph-json/` (readable JSON codec). These are the **only** committed stores of a project; the live `.sdd/graph/` is gitignored ([DEC-001](../decisions/DEC-001-committed-store.md)). Run it on purpose (M06a, M99, before a release); the committed copy lags the docs until the next run. Steps:
  1. **Checkpoint.** Without a daemon: open the store writable (`daemon_running` if another process holds it), checkpoint, close. With a daemon: no checkpoint, because `relate clone` reads every committed transaction.
  2. **Copies.** Delete the old `graph/`, `graph.rl` and `graph-json/` under `--out` (nothing else there). With the `relate` CLI on PATH (O3, closed: only the CLI can clone; it works beside a running daemon): `relate clone` for all three. Without it: a plain directory copy of `graph/` only when no daemon runs, and `graph.rl` and `graph-json/` are `skipped`; with a daemon and no CLI the command fails with `daemon_running` and says to install the CLI or stop the daemon. `:memory:` is `invalid_input`.
  3. **Verify.** The live store and every copy are opened read-only and their node and relationship counts per label and type compared; a mismatch is an error.
  4. **Result** `{out, copies: {graph, graph_rl, graph_json}, relate_cli, checkpointed, total_nodes, total_relationships}`, each copy `written` or `skipped`.

properties.title: Security

properties.text:
- **Local daemon:** the risk is another local process or a web page in the user's browser writing to the graph or the Markdown. Mitigations: loopback bind, optional token, Origin checks.
- **Hosted demo:** the internet. The risk is writes, resource exhaustion through heavy Cypher, and reaching the home server's other services. Mitigations: a separate read-only process, a query guard, limits, an isolated container network, Cloudflare in front.
- Out of scope: multi-user auth, untrusted Markdown authors (the repo owner writes the docs).
properties.title: Threat model

properties.text:
1. Binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Binding anything else requires `SDD_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` **and** `SDD_TOKEN`, or the daemon refuses to start. **Exception inside a container** (`/.dockerenv` exists): `SDD_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` alone is enough, because the container must bind `0.0.0.0` and our Compose files publish the port on `127.0.0.1` only ([SPEC-11 §2](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#2-compose)).
2. `SDD_TOKEN` (optional locally): when set, every `/mcp` and `/api` request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or gets 401 `unauthorized`. `daemon.json` stores only its SHA-256. **The dashboard under a token:** its static files hold no data and need no token. On the first 401 the dashboard asks for the token once, keeps it in `sessionStorage` (this tab only, gone when it closes) and sends it as the header on every `/api` call. `EventSource` cannot send headers, so with a token set the Board uses its polling fallback ([SPEC-07 §3](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md#3-live-events)). The token never goes in a URL or a cookie.
3. **Host check (DNS rebinding):** every request's `Host` header must name a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, any port) or a host listed in `SDD_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; otherwise 403 `forbidden_host`. Without it, a web page whose domain re-resolves to 127.0.0.1 could read the whole API, because reads have no Origin check.
4. **Write endpoints and `/mcp` reject requests whose `Origin` header is not the daemon's own origin** (stops a web page from posting to localhost) with 403 `forbidden_origin`. "Own origin" is `http://<the request's Host header>`, which the Host check has already limited to loopback, so it works behind a Compose port mapping. Requests without `Origin` (Claude Code, the CLI) are allowed.
5. Write-back only edits files inside the project root, resolved with `Path.resolve()`. A path outside it is `invalid_input`.
6. Logs never contain the token or full Markdown text; section IDs only.
properties.title: Local daemon

properties.text:
Used by the `query` tool, `POST /api/query` and `sdd query`.

1. **Tokenise** the statement (skipping strings and comments) and reject it with `query_rejected` if it contains `CREATE`, `MERGE`, `SET`, `DELETE`, `DETACH`, `REMOVE`, `DROP`, `LOAD`, `FOREACH`, `CALL`, `USE`, `IN TRANSACTIONS`, or more than one statement.
2. **Run it in a transaction that is always rolled back** (`autocommit = False` … `rollback()`), so a write that slips past step 1 still changes nothing. This layer is load-bearing: a `read_only=True` connection accepts a write inside a transaction and refuses it only at commit (O11). It runs on a `read_only=True` snapshot connection where one is available (always in public mode; in the daemon if open item O12 allows, [SPEC-01 §4](SPEC-01-architecture.md#4-relate-access-and-concurrency)), a third layer that also keeps it off the writer's lock.
3. Cap rows at 100 (`truncated: true` beyond). Time limit 5 s: `relate-db` offers no per-query timeout (O4, closed), so the query runs on a worker thread and the request fails with `query_timeout` after 5 s while the result is discarded. Python cannot kill that thread, so at most **one** guarded query runs at a time per process; a second one waits up to 5 s, then gets `query_timeout`.
4. Variable-length patterns without an upper bound (`*`, `*2..`) are rejected **in every mode**, daemon included, because a runaway query blocks claims; the maximum is `*..4`.
5. `SDD_PUBLIC_QUERY` = `guarded` (default) or `presets` (only preset names run; the box is display-only).
properties.title: Query guard

properties.text:
`sdd public` is a different process from the daemon:
- Opens the store with `read_only=True` and reopens when `manifest.json` changes ([SPEC-01 §1](SPEC-01-architecture.md#1-process-model)).
- Serves only the endpoints marked public in [SPEC-07 §2](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md#2-endpoint-index). Write endpoints return 403 `read_only`; `/mcp` is not mounted at all (404).
- Rate limit in-process: 60 requests/min per IP for `/api/query`, 600/min for the rest (Cloudflare adds its own rules); over the limit, 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`. The client IP comes from `CF-Connecting-IP` (then `X-Forwarded-For`) **only** for requests from the trusted proxy network `SDD_TRUSTED_PROXY_NET` (set to `COMPOSE_SUBNET` in [SPEC-11 §7](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#7-home-hosting)); otherwise from the socket.
- Response headers: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
- Error responses never include stack traces or file system paths outside the project.
properties.title: Public mode

properties.text:
- Containers run as a non-root user with a read-only root file system (the store volume excepted, plus a `tmpfs` at `/tmp`; `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`), `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`, CPU and memory limits (`public`: 1 CPU, 512 MB; `replay`: 1 CPU, 768 MB).
- The hosted stack runs as its own Compose project (`relate-sdd`) with its own fixed subnet, separate from the server's other stacks. Only `public` publishes a port, on `PUBLIC_BIND` (loopback by default). `replay` and `cloudflared` publish none.
- TLS ends at Cloudflare; Relate's own servers are plaintext and are not used for the public demo.
- The replay writer works on a copy of the sample project in a volume, never on the repo checkout.
properties.title: Hosted demo infrastructure

properties.text:
1. Outside a container, the daemon refuses to start with `--host 0.0.0.0` unless `SDD_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` and `SDD_TOKEN` are set; inside one, `SDD_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` is enough.
2. With `SDD_TOKEN` set, `/api/status` without the header returns 401; with it, 200. `/` and the dashboard's static files still return 200, and the dashboard, given the token once, loads the Board (by polling).
3. `POST /api/tasks/M01.1/claim` with `Origin: https://evil.example` returns 403.
4. The guard rejects `MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n`, `CREATE (:X)`, `MATCH (n) SET n.x = 1`, `CALL db.labels()`, and two statements separated by `;`; it accepts `MATCH (n:Task) RETURN n.id LIMIT 5`.
5. A write that bypasses the tokenizer (simulated in a test by disabling step 1) leaves the store unchanged.
6. A query running longer than 5 s returns `query_timeout`, and the server stays responsive.
7. In public mode, `/mcp` returns 404 and every write endpoint returns 403.
8. A daemon request with `Host: evil.example` returns 403 `forbidden_host`; `Host: localhost:8770` with `Origin: http://localhost:8770` may write.
9. In daemon mode, the guard rejects `MATCH p=(a)-[*]->(b) RETURN p` and accepts `MATCH p=(a)-[*..4]->(b) RETURN p LIMIT 5`.

properties.title: Testing and benchmark

properties.text:
- pytest. Every numbered acceptance check in a spec becomes a test named after it: `test_spec05_ac03_double_claim_one_winner`. One test per check (more if needed, same prefix). Plain names for extra tests.
- Files by spec: `tests/spec03/test_parse_*.py`, `tests/spec05/…`; invariants in `tests/invariants/`.
- This naming also feeds the tool itself: on this repo, `TESTS` relationships link our tests to our own spec checks (dogfooding).
- Assert on error `code`, never on `message` text.
- Never mock Relate or the write queue. Mock only time (`freezegun`-style clock injected through `config`) and, for the benchmark's optional exact count, the HTTP client.
properties.title: Conventions

properties.text:
- `project` fixture: copies a fixture repo into `tmp_path`, optionally `git init`s it with scripted commits (git CLI, no network).
- `store` fixture: a real Relate directory store in `tmp_path` (`graph.store.Store`), with the [SPEC-02 §6](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#6-indexes-and-constraints) schema applied; closed (queue drained, checkpointed) after the test.
- `app` fixture: the daemon's Starlette app on a real store, driven through Starlette's `TestClient` (in-process, no sockets). `public_app` does the same in public mode.
- Watcher tests use `SDD_WATCH=poll` with a 0.1 s interval.
- Concurrency tests use real threads against the real write queue.
- `pytest-socket` blocks the network; the in-process client needs none.
properties.title: Test host

properties.text:
`tests/fixtures/` holds small repos **written to mirror each reference format, with invented content**. Nothing is copied from the reference projects (office-suite-v2 cannot be made public, open item O1); only their conventions are reproduced:
- `rag_style/`: office-rag conventions (`` ## 2. `documents` `` schema tables, `**Status:**` then text, `docs/deviations/` empty, root and nested CLAUDE.md).
- `suite_style/`: office-suite-v2 conventions (`**Spec ID:**` headers, `### attachments` tables with `→ users [restrict]`, letter-suffixed milestones, `**Status: DONE (…)**` paragraphs, plan files, nested `> > **DEVIATION:**` notes, legacy task lines without IDs).
- `tool_style/`: this tool's own conventions (task IDs, `(after …)`, Feature lines), plus code files, tests named after checks, and a scripted git history.
properties.title: Fixtures

properties.text:
`tests/invariants/` grows every milestone:
1. `relate` is imported only in `graph/store.py` (also an import-linter contract).
2. **Rebuild equivalence:** `sdd sync --reset` on a synced project reproduces every node and relationship except graph-only state ([SPEC-02 §2](SPEC-02-graph-schema.md#graph-only-state-canonical-list)). The comparison excludes Agent and Event nodes; `CLAIMED`, `ABOUT` and every `src = "tool"` relationship; the graph-only Task properties; `last_synced`, Section `changed_at` and `Meta.last_full_sync`; and the derived `status` of tasks that were claimed and of their milestone.
3. Upserts change the graph-only Task properties (`claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, `completed_by`, `done_at`, `notes`) only in the cases of [SPEC-04 §2.1](SPEC-04-sync.md#21-task-upsert-rules), and never delete a relationship with `src = "tool"` (except the `CLAIMED` relationship that a hand tick clears, SPEC-04 §2.1).
4. Write-back changes exactly the intended lines (diff check) and preserves line endings.
5. Public mode: no route outside the public list answers, and `/mcp` is absent (built from the route table, so new routes are covered automatically).
6. **Doc ↔ code drift:** the MCP tools in [SPEC-05 §2](SPEC-05-agent-tools.md#2-tool-index), the endpoints in [SPEC-07 §2](SPEC-07-dashboard-and-api.md#2-endpoint-index) and the commands in [SPEC-08 §2](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#2-commands) match what the code registers. The test parses our own specs with our own parser.
7. The query guard rejects every write clause in a fixed corpus.
properties.title: Invariant suite

properties.text: `sdd bench` measures what the graph saves, deterministically, so judges can reproduce it. Results go to `bench/results/<date>.json` and `.md` (the README table).
properties.title: Benchmark

properties.text:
For every task in the chosen milestones of the sample project:
- **Markdown baseline (the token rule as practised today):** root CLAUDE.md + the whole milestone file + each *Read first* target (whole file when marked, otherwise the referenced sections' line ranges, as `grep -n '^## '` + Read would load them) + `DEVIATIONS.md` + every deviation file amending a read section + the plan file if one exists.
- **Graph, `detail="milestone"`:** the same sections from `get_context`, without the surrounding files.
- **Graph, `detail="task"`:** the default packet.

Reported per task and averaged: characters and estimated tokens (chars ÷ 4). `--exact` uses the Anthropic token-counting API when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (never in tests).
properties.title: Context per task

properties.text:
"What changed since my last session?" after a scripted set of edits (two section edits, one deviation, three completed tasks):
- **Baseline:** re-reading CLAUDE.md, the active milestone, `DEVIATIONS.md` and every Markdown file changed since (by git).
- **Graph:** one `what_changed` result.
properties.title: Session restart

properties.text:
`sdd bench collisions --agents 10 --tasks 30`:
- **Naive:** 10 threads each tick their own box with read-modify-write of the same milestone file, with small random delays. Count lost ticks.
- **Graph:** the same 10 agents through `claim_task` / `complete_task`. Count double claims and lost ticks (expected: 0 and 0).
properties.title: Parallel collisions

properties.text: Two real Claude Code runs of the same milestone on a copy of the sample, one with the plain workflow and one with the MCP tools, comparing the tokens recorded in the session transcripts. Reported separately and labelled as a single run, not a benchmark.
properties.title: Live run (optional, stretch)

properties.text: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --strict src/sdd`, `lint-imports`, `pytest -q` (which includes a smoke test that every dashboard file is served and references no external URL). All run in the dev container ([SPEC-11 §1](SPEC-11-deployment-and-demo.md#1-development-container)) and in GitHub Actions.
properties.title: Gates

properties.text:
1. `pytest -q` passes in the dev container with the network blocked.
2. The invariant suite contains items 1–7 above and passes.
3. `sdd bench context` on the sample project prints the per-task table and writes the JSON and Markdown results.
4. `sdd bench collisions` reports lost ticks > 0 for naive (over 5 runs) and exactly 0 double claims and 0 lost ticks for the graph.

The invariant suite contains items 1–7 above and passes.

properties.header_json: {"Owner of": "the Dockerfile and Compose files, the development container, home hosting, sprint replay, the sample project, the static demo, the submission checklist", "Status": "v1 (2026-11-21)"}
properties.owner_of: the Dockerfile and Compose files, the development container, home hosting, sprint replay, the sample project, the static demo, the submission checklist
properties.title: Deployment and demo

properties.text:
All building, testing and running happens in Docker. The Windows host's C: drive is nearly full; Docker's data lives on D:, so images, volumes and caches stay off C:.

- `Dockerfile`, stage **`dev`**: `python:3.13-slim` (glibc; `relate-db` has no musllinux wheel) + `git`, `curl`, `ca-certificates`, `openssh-client`, `uv` (copied from `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv`), the Relate CLI (official install script into `HOME=/opt/relate`, linked onto `PATH`; amd64 + arm64; how and why: O9 in [SPEC-00 §8](SPEC-00-overview.md#8-schedule-and-open-items)), `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (turns off the CLI's default-on telemetry), and `git config --system --add safe.directory '*'` (system level, so it also applies to other users).
- `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv`, so the virtualenv lives in a **named volume**, not on the bind mount (fast, and no Windows/Linux venv clash). `UV_CACHE_DIR=/cache/uv` in another named volume. `UV_LINK_MODE=copy`.
- `SDD_WATCH=poll` (inotify misses host edits through the bind mount).
- Usage:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d dev                 # long-running dev container
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec dev uv sync          # deps into /opt/venv
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec dev uv run pytest -q
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec dev uv run sdd daemon --host 0.0.0.0   # :8770 on host loopback
```
properties.title: Development container

properties.text:
| File | For | Services |
|---|---|---|
| `docker-compose.dev.yml` | Development | `dev` (bind mount `.:/workspace`, volumes `venv`, `uvcache`, port `127.0.0.1:8770:8770`, `command: sleep infinity`) |
| `docker-compose.yml` | **Judges**: `docker compose up` | `sample`: the runtime image running `sdd demo serve` (prepare, then the daemon; [SPEC-08 §2](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#2-commands)) on a copy of the sample project in a volume, port `127.0.0.1:8770:8770`. Dashboard at `http://localhost:8770` |
| `deploy/docker-compose.yml` | Home server ([§7](#7-home-hosting)) | `replay` (writer, [§4](#4-sprint-replay)), `public` (`sdd public`, store volume mounted read-only), `cloudflared` (profile `tunnel`) |

Inside containers the daemon binds `0.0.0.0` with `SDD_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`; the root Compose files publish every port on `127.0.0.1` only ([SPEC-09 §2](SPEC-09-security.md#2-local-daemon)). All long-running services: `restart: unless-stopped`, a healthcheck, and the limits in [SPEC-09 §5](SPEC-09-security.md#5-hosted-demo-infrastructure). Services with HTTP (`sample`, `public`) check `/api/health`. `replay` has no HTTP server: it touches `/data/run/.sdd/replay.heartbeat` every tick, and its healthcheck passes when that file exists and is younger than 30 s.
properties.title: Compose

properties.text: Stage **`build`**: `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable` into `/opt/venv` (non-editable, so the venv does not point back at the build stage's source tree). Stage **`runtime`**: `python:3.13-slim` + `git` (for git sync) + `/opt/venv` + `src/` + `samples/`; non-root user `sdd` (uid 10001); `ENTRYPOINT ["sdd"]`; no image-level `HEALTHCHECK` (it depends on the command, so each Compose service sets its own, [§2](#2-compose)). Target size < 250 MB. Builds for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
properties.title: Runtime image

properties.text:
`sdd demo replay --sample samples/<name> --data /data` makes the hosted demo move:

1. **Prepare:** copy the sample's working tree and history into `/data/run` (a fresh git repo from the sample's bundle, [§5](#5-sample-project)) and apply its `replay.toml` start state (which milestones start unticked).
2. **Run** in-process (the replay process owns `/data/run/.sdd/graph`): one orchestrator and three workers named `opus-orch`, `sonnet-1…3`. Every tick (`SDD_REPLAY_TICK`, default 4 s) an idle worker calls `next_tasks` → `claim_task`; a busy worker finishes after 2–5 ticks with `complete_task` (notes and files from `replay.toml`, or generated from the task's governed sections). Deviations scripted in `replay.toml` are logged on their tasks with `log_deviation`. When a milestone's tasks are done, the orchestrator calls `complete_milestone`.
3. **Checkpoint** after every write, so `public` sees it on its next reopen (≤ 2 s).
4. **Loop:** when the scripted milestones are done or after `SDD_REPLAY_MAX_MIN` (default 20) minutes, pause 30 s, reset to step 1, and continue. Deterministic with `--seed`.
properties.title: Sprint replay

properties.text:
`samples/courtside/` is the project judges explore: **Courtside**, a court-booking app for a community sports hall (badminton and tennis courts), built by three invented people (Nadia Okafor, Tomás Reyes, Mei Lin Chua, `@courtside.example`). It is **invented**: office-suite-v2 cannot be made public (open item O1, closed "no"; [DEC-004](../decisions/DEC-004-sample-fallback.md)), so no text, file name, commit message or structure specific to it is copied. Only its *conventions* are used, which are generic.

- **Format:** the office-suite conventions (`**Spec ID:**` headers, `### <table>` schema tables with `→ <table> [restrict]`, letter-suffixed milestones, `**Status: DONE (…)**` paragraphs, plan files, nested `> > **DEVIATION:**` notes), plus this tool's conventions (task IDs, `(after …)`, Feature lines). It grows out of the `suite_style` fixture ([SPEC-10 §3](SPEC-10-testing-and-benchmark.md#3-fixtures)).
- **Size:** about 6 specs (one schema spec with 6–8 tables), 8 milestones (some done, some letter-suffixed, one with a plan file), about 6 deviations, and a code tree of small placeholder files grouped by feature, so Feature globs, `explain` and `find_code` have something to show.
- **History:** `scripts/make_sample.py` scripts a linear git history (as `samples/<name>.bundle`) that builds the milestones in order, with commits naming their tasks (`[M03.2]`), so `COMPLETES`, `TOUCHES` and `explain` have real data.
- **Story by design:** the centrepiece table is `bookings`: defined in SPEC-02 §3, used by SPEC-03, 04, 05 and 06 and their features, written by tasks of M02, M03a, M03b, M04 and M05a, affected by four deviations (D002, D003, D005, D006), and tested through SPEC-02's checks, so `sdd impact bookings` fills every group (specs, sections, tables, features, files, open and done tasks, deviations, tests, commits) with `via` chains (SPEC-00 §7 item 5). Some milestones are left unticked in `replay.toml` for the live replay ([§4](#4-sprint-replay)).
- **Files:** the sample's final files are `samples/courtside/` (docs, code, `CLAUDE.md` with a generated status block). `make_sample.py` replays about forty commits (fixed authors and dates, so the SHAs never change) into a temp repository, checks that its tip tree equals the folder byte for byte, and bundles it as `samples/courtside.bundle`; the repository root's `.sddignore` lists `samples/`, so this repo's own graph never walks it. It then syncs a clone of the bundle, so git sync sees the history even though `samples/courtside/` is a sub-folder of this repository, and fails unless `sdd doctor` on the sample shows zero warnings, `impact bookings` fills every group and no temp path is in `graph.json`.
- **Store:** `make_sample.py` finally runs `sdd sync` and `sdd snapshot` on the sample (the built store is `samples/courtside/.sdd/graph/`, the copies are `samples/courtside/.sdd/snapshots/{graph/, graph.rl, graph-json/}`). Its `.sdd/graph/` is a build output that no daemon ever runs on (judges' Compose and the replay work on a copy in a volume), so it is committed as is, with the snapshot copies ([SPEC-08 §3](SPEC-08-cli-and-exports.md#3-exports-and-snapshots), [DEC-001](../decisions/DEC-001-committed-store.md)).

This repo's own `docs/` and store are a second, smaller example (dogfooding).

properties.title: Home hosting

properties.text:
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, with `name: relate-sdd` so it never clashes with other stacks on the server (office-suite runs as `office-suite`).
- `deploy/.env.example`, committed, placeholders only; copied to `deploy/.env` (gitignored by M00a.1):

```bash
# Copy to deploy/.env (git-ignored) and replace every CHANGE_ME. Placeholders only: never commit real values.

# Images (built on the server from this repo: `docker compose build`)
IMAGE_PREFIX=relate-sdd
IMAGE_TAG=local
# The compose network, and the only network `public` trusts for CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For.
# Must differ from other stacks on the host (office-suite uses 172.30.0.0/24).
COMPOSE_SUBNET=172.31.0.0/24

# The public HTTPS hostname (shown in the dashboard footer and used for absolute links)
PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://CHANGE_ME.example.com
# Optional host port for `public`, for checking it on the server or for an existing tunnel that
# reaches services through the host. Loopback by default; never 0.0.0.0 unless the LAN may see it.
PUBLIC_BIND=127.0.0.1
PUBLIC_PORT=8780

# Demo behaviour
SAMPLE=CHANGE_ME                  # folder name under samples/
SDD_PUBLIC_QUERY=guarded          # guarded | presets
SDD_REPLAY_TICK=4
SDD_REPLAY_MAX_MIN=20
SDD_REPLAY_SEED=42
TZ=UTC

# Cloudflare tunnel (remotely managed): the token from Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels.
# Start with `docker compose --profile tunnel up -d`.
TUNNEL_TOKEN=
CLOUDFLARED_VERSION=2026.10.3
```

No other secrets: the hosted demo has no database, no accounts and no write path.
properties.title: Files

properties.text:
| Service | Image | Networks | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `replay` | `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/sdd:${IMAGE_TAG}` | `default` | `sdd demo replay`; volume `demo-data` read-write; the only writer |
| `public` | same image | `default` | `sdd public --store /data/run/.sdd/graph`; `demo-data` mounted **read-only**; `ports: ['${PUBLIC_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${PUBLIC_PORT:-8780}:8780']`; healthcheck on `/api/health`; `depends_on: replay` (healthy) |
| `cloudflared` | `cloudflare/cloudflared:${CLOUDFLARED_VERSION}` | `default` | `profiles: ['tunnel']`, `command: ['tunnel', '--no-autoupdate', 'run']`, `TUNNEL_TOKEN` from `.env`; no ports |

`default` has the fixed subnet `${COMPOSE_SUBNET}`. `public` takes the client IP for rate limiting from `CF-Connecting-IP` **only** when the request comes from that subnet, otherwise from the socket. So nobody on the LAN can pick the IP the rate limiter sees ([SPEC-09 §4](SPEC-09-security.md#4-public-mode)). Hardening and limits: [SPEC-09 §5](SPEC-09-security.md#5-hosted-demo-infrastructure).
properties.title: Services

properties.text:
1. On the server: `git clone` this repo, `cd deploy`, `cp .env.example .env`, fill it in.
2. `docker compose build` then `docker compose up -d`; check `curl http://127.0.0.1:8780/api/health` shows `mode: public`.
3. Cloudflare Zero Trust → Tunnels → create a tunnel (Docker connector), copy its token into `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, then `docker compose --profile tunnel up -d`.
4. Tunnel → Public hostname: `CHANGE_ME.example.com` → service `http://public:8780`.
   **If the server already runs a shared cloudflared** for other apps, skip the `tunnel` profile and point that tunnel at `http://<server-host>:8780` instead (set `PUBLIC_BIND` to an address it can reach), or attach its container to this stack's network.
5. Cloudflare rules: rate-limit `POST /api/query` (e.g. 30/min per IP), cache the dashboard's assets by extension (`.js`, `.css`, `.svg`: the dashboard is served at `/`, not under a `/static/` prefix; never `/api/*`, and not `/` itself so a deploy shows at once), and turn on Bot Fight Mode. SSE (`/api/events`) passes through tunnels; the dashboard falls back to polling if a proxy buffers it.
6. Update: `git pull && docker compose build && docker compose up -d`. The replay resets itself, so no data migration is needed.

The README links **"Live demo (home-hosted) · Static demo (GitHub Pages, always up)"**. Judging may run weeks past the deadline, which is why the static demo exists.

Their content does not matter, and a read-only open never creates them, so a copy without them cannot be opened read-only on a read-only mount or by `sdd public`. `.cypherlite.writer` is not needed and is recreated by any writable open.
